notes.title: It’s time to assemble your perfect grip car!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

In [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master [/b][/url], speed is of the utmost importance, however we all must know how to use it wisely. For example, when drifting, taking your foot off the gas can help you maintain better control or steer clear of obstacles. The same applies to mountain pass roads, where rushing too fast can cause you to veer off course.

However, there are cases where the [b]highest possible speed is most desirable[/b]. Grip races are a perfect example – in these events, the only thing that matters is the time it takes to complete the track, so you need to extract every ounce of power from your car. And you know what? We are about to tell you exactly how to do that. 

[h3]Check out the Grip Tuning Presentation video:[/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
[previewyoutube=ToKYCzPRjoY;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]How to Tune a Grip Car?[/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
Similar to the previous “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410?emclan=103582791473542743&emgid=545606206552539160]Tuning Guide[/url]”, it’s worth noting that each driver has a unique playstyle and preferences, which is why we encourage you to experiment with various combinations and settings.

With that in mind, the following hints should be taken more as a suggestion than a ready-made recipe for success. However, this doesn’t mean we can’t rely on a [b]few proven tricks[/b]! Luckily, among grip experts, there are tried-and-true techniques that can significantly improve your chances when facing off against other drivers. Let’s take a look!
[list]
[*] [b]Engine[/b]: In this step, there is no room for half-measures. We will need the best possible ECU, strong Intake and Exhaust, and the most powerful Internals you can afford. Same goes for the Boost - the more advanced, the better.
[*][b] Suspension[/b]: We need it low and stable. Not only to enhance our car with an awesome, bold look, but also to ensure better grip on the road. You are sure to appreciate them, when you hit those impressive, near-top speeds. Aim for stiffer sway bars variants. Adjustable control arms are an option but are not necessary as they can do more harm than good in some setups.
[*] [b]Powertrain[/b]: Be sure to try out the dedicated, sport clutch. Just like with the control arms, an adjustable gearbox is not necessary, but you can play around with the gear ratios to better suit your preferences. On the other hand, an adjustable differential is recommended, but as a starting point the stock one will do the trick.
[*] [b]Brakes and Tires[/b]: Make no mistake, brakes are extremely important in grip races. Choose the best possible variant! When it comes to tires, we strive to achieve the best grip - this is the most important feature you should pay attention to.
[*] [b]Nitrous[/b]: Do we even need to say a word? 🔥😈
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/dd7d6836d6142ff606f91b0c2712eb63117b1d7c.png[/img]
[h3]The new parts are just the beginning. Now it's time to fine-tune them all![/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
Now that your dream car is equipped with top-of-the-line equipment, we can move on to setting things up. Keep in mind that perfecting your car’s setup doesn’t happen overnight, so don’t stress if things don’t click right away. Mastery comes with trial, error, and plenty of fine-tuning; however, we’re confident you’ll get there. And now, let’s cut to the chase and get to work, shall we?

Let’s start with height. Our goal with the up-and-down adjustment is to achieve a clean fit between the wheels and the arches. Try to find that one sweet spot to avoid both rubbing and an overly raised chassis. Next, stick to the “more tire - more traction” rule, and pick the widest possible rims and tires. Simple as that! 

As for the turning range and, the standard one is completely sufficient. Last but not least - wheel alignment - you want to keep as much surface area of the tire on the road, so look for neutral camber values of around 0,0. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/75d4b41581d608c111539bae126e2bb7d8c3739c.png[/img]
[h3]Ready to hit the gas?[/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
We hope you had fun diving into the world of grip-focused tuning in JDM: Japanese Drift Master! Our aim is to strike the perfect balance between realism and ease-of-use so players of all levels can experience the excitement of building and fine-tuning their dream car. We simply can't wait to see your grip beasts on the road and hear the legends of your awesome racing deeds. Speed ​​records - your time is over!

notes.title: Let’s tune your ultimate drift car
notes.notes:
[b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] delivers [b]a true simcade experience[/b], allowing you to explore the scenic roads of Guntama at your own pace. Whether you prefer to cruise leisurely, dive into the story of Touma and his friends, or fine-tune your ride to dominate the drift and grip scenes, the game offers something for every driving enthusiast.

Tuning your car can feel overwhelming at first, given the [b]wide range of customizable parts and performance stats[/b] you can tweak, but no worries - we got you! To make things more straightforward, we’ve created a [b]video guide[/b] to help you navigate the tuning shops and build your perfect machine.

[h2]Check out the Drift Tuning Presentation video:[/h2]
[hr] [/hr]
[previewyoutube=kJn9CzBuY2o;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]How to Tune a Drift Car [/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
We are aware that each driver has their own unique playstyle and preferences, so we encourage you to experiment with different combinations and settings. Adapting a car for drifting involves many variables, but a few core rules always hold true - you can think of them as a base during your fine-tuning adventure. What are they?
[list]
[*] For optimal drifting performance, you’ll want to maximize horsepower and torque. In fact, you can never have too much power, especially when you lose some of your speed through heavy friction. And while the engine follows the rule of "the stronger, the better", the suspension setup is where the real magic happens. 
[*] Lowering the suspension is the best way to increase stability when drifting. The same goes for stiffer suspension variants, which will provide a grounded, road-hugging sensation while keeping tilting and rocking to a minimum.
[*] Invest in a proper angle kit, being an essential element during long, deep drifts and maximize your turning range. 
[*] The wheel alignment and tilt adjustments are so unique and varied as drivers of Guntama themselves. Do not hesitate to experiment, although if you'd like, you can back up your decisions with these suggestions: negative tilt for the front wheels and slight toe-out alignment near-zero degrees for the rear wheels. [/list]
Do you still feel like you need more specific information and examples? Be sure to take advantage of the sample drifting setup down below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8b7e811746cf2ab260441f9cdff63e3b5d302eff.png[/img]

[h3]Sample drifting setup - ready for you to use and modify![/h3]
[hr] [/hr]
[b]Handling: [/b]
[list]
[*] Use Fully Adjustable Coilover Suspension, stiffer sway bars and adjustable control arms to fine-tune your wheel angles.
[*] Choose a professional steering system (angle kit) to maximize turning range.
[*] A welded differential is recommended for maintaining a consistent drift.
[*] Nitrous has minimal impact on drift handling (such insights will mainly benefit the most experienced players and are tailored to their personal preferences), so focus on suspension and steering instead. On the other hand, you may want to mount larger, more powerful brakes. [/list]
[b]Suspension Height:[/b]
[list]
[*] Lower the car, so the wheels sit just inside the wheel arches, but ensure they don’t rub when driving. This change will grant you more stability on the road.
[*] Stiffen the suspension to prevent excessive body roll, but don't overdo it. For drifting, a more balanced suspension setup that allows for controlled body roll and weight transfer is generally preferred, as it helps to maintain the balance between traction and slip, making the car more responsive to throttle inputs. [/list]
[b]Wheels and Alignment:[/b]
[list]
[*] Front wheels: Tilt them to around -3 degrees for better turn-in response.
[*] Rear wheels: The rule here is simple - if you have tuned a car with much horsepower, keep them close to 0 degrees to maintain the best traction.
[*] Wheel alignment: Slightly toe-out (-0.2) the front wheels and toe-in (+0.1) the rear wheels.  [/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/bc597b71752af4a2422cdbcc8d6562eb9db21fa8.png[/img]

[h3]Put your garage to good use[/h3]
We hope you enjoyed this look at [b]drift-oriented car tuning[/b] and picked up some valuable tips on modifying your car in [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b]! Our goal is to provide a realistic yet accessible tuning system, ensuring that all players - whether newcomers or seasoned enthusiasts - can enjoy the thrill of customization and performance optimization. No matter what challenges you take on in the game, you’ll have the tools to build an incredible machine that suits your playstyle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/d327c33f63fe401c583f440e3529a3eb51262316.gif[/img]

If you have any questions about tuning mechanics, feel free to ask in the comments or join our Discord server, where our team is always excited to welcome new members to the community. notes.title: Let’s Reminisce!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

From the initial concept to the final version, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] has come a long way. As we created new gameplay features and showcased exciting updates, we couldn’t help but reflect on the incredible journey this project has taken. Built by true enthusiasts, JDM is a game crafted with passion and dedication to bring an authentic drifting experience to life.

[h3]Check out the video and see how the gameplay has evolved over the years:[/h3]

[previewyoutube=bCtm25zRjR0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Concept[/h3]
From the start, our goal was to create a simcade racing game that would introduce the art of drifting to a wider audience. Inspired by titles like [i]Initial D[/i] and [i]Fast & Furious: Tokyo Drift[/i], we envisioned a story-driven experience. However, the way we wanted to present that story evolved significantly over time.

Initially, we explored a Visual Novel-style approach with character illustrations, but we soon sought a way to make the narrative feel more mature and immersive. You can read more about this evolution in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/4165345236042311740?l][b]our devlog on concept art[/b][/url].

Developing the gameplay and open-world map was a challenge, but having a [b]strong foundation in physics kept us focused on our vision[/b]. With simcade driving mechanics as our core, we never lost sight of what we wanted to create.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/207a12945eced46ff9feb10fd828cdf587b5d479.png[/img]
[h3]The First Demo[/h3]
[b]Steam Next Fest 2023[/b] was the first opportunity for players to download and experience JDM: Japanese Drift Master firsthand. The response was incredible—our game ranked [b]#1 in daily active players among all of the showcased demos[/b]! We were thrilled by the overwhelming attention and invaluable feedback from the community.

This first demo only featured a small portion of the open-world map that will be available in the full version, but the love for the Japanese countryside setting was undeniable. Players embraced the atmosphere, and their insights helped us refine and improve the game even further.

The demo was live for four months and was downloaded [b]over 750,000 times[/b]! With such an amazing response, we were more motivated than ever to keep pushing forward and turn JDM into the ultimate racing adventure you’ve been dreaming of!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/25ad9e782f96b2f0c5f6af544868b99e85231db4.jpg[/img]
[h3]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/h3]
In [b]August 2024[/b], we launched a demo-prologue that introduced a storyline for the first time! Players got to experience the origin story of Hatori ‘Scorpion’ Hasashi, one of the key rivals in the full version of the game, where they will face off against the main character, [b]Touma[/b]. This free prologue not only showcased our refined driving mechanics but also gave players access to a [b]larger portion of the map[/b] and our unique [b]manga-inspired storytelling[/b].

With later updates, we introduced [b]Challenge Mode[/b], which kept the game thriving for months. Players honed their drifting and racing skills, competing in monthly leaderboards where we crowned the top drifters and grippers.

Throughout this time, we gathered valuable feedback on the story, gameplay, and optimization, all of which played a crucial role in polishing the [b]upcoming full version[/b].

Originally born in Europe, this high-energy dance music became synonymous with the thrill of street racing, thanks to the Internet and countless videos pairing its fast beats with drifting action. The legendary anime[i] Initial D [/i]cemented its place in car culture, making Eurobeat an essential part of the Japanese drifting scene.

That’s why[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b] JDM: Japanese Drift Master [/b][/url]wouldn’t be complete without it. We want players to truly feel the intensity and adrenaline of drifting, accompanied by a soundtrack they already associate with racing games and Japanese street racing in general. [h3]Nissan Takes the Spotlight in JDM: Japanese Drift Master![/h3]
We’ve brought together a lineup of fan-favorite Nissan models, beloved in both motorsports and pop culture, including:
[list]
[*] [b]Nissan R34[/b] – a legend that continues to captivate car lovers around the world.
[*] [b]Nissan Fairlady[/b] – a lightweight, well-balanced machine with a timeless design.
[*] [b]Nissan 350Z[/b] – beloved icon and Nissan’s Z legacy.
[/list]And that’s just the beginning! This is just a sneak peek at the cars that will add life and excitement to the open world of JDM: Japanese Drift Master. Read along to learn more about what makes these models so special!

[h3]Nissan R34[/h3]
Also known as the [b]Nissan Skyline GT-R[/b], the R34 is one of the most legendary JDM cars ever produced, celebrated for its advanced technology, striking design, and dominance on both the streets and the track. Its [b]twin-turbocharged 2.6-liter inline-six RB26DETT engine[/b] offered incredible tuning and racing potential—especially impressive for the 1990s.

The Nissan R34 was equipped with an advanced [b]Multi-Function Display (MFD)[/b], providing drivers with real-time performance data such as [b]boost pressure, oil temperature, and even lap times[/b].

Thanks to its appearances in [b]movies and video games[/b], the R34 has been immortalized for car enthusiasts around the world, securing its place as an automotive icon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ec19637dd5f37b53b55f4020566009245f5ef2b9.png[/img]
[h3]Nissan Fairlady[/h3]
Known outside Japan as the [b]Datsun/Nissan Z series[/b], the Fairlady is one of the most iconic sports car lines ever produced. Nissan aimed to create a [b]budget-friendly sports car[/b] that could rival European legends like Jaguar and Porsche, resulting in a dream machine for JDM lovers.

With its [b]3.0L V6 twin-turbo engine and futuristic design[/b], the Fairlady became one of the most [b]innovative and performance-driven[/b] sports cars of its time.

The name ‘[b]Fairlady[/b]’ was inspired by the Broadway musical [i]My Fair Lady[/i], reflecting Nissan’s vision of [b]elegance and global appeal[/b]. Its appearances in movies and video games further solidified its status as a [b]symbol of JDM heritage, innovation, and driving excitement[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/541ab93523557c7af42e6802b20515c9349fcf38.png[/img]
[h3]Nissan 350Z[/h3]
Also known as the [b]Fairlady Z (Z33)[/b] in Japan, the 350Z was a game-changer in the early 2000s, bringing back the legendary [b]Z-series[/b] after a hiatus. It quickly became a favorite among enthusiasts, tuners, and drifters worldwide.

Powered by the [b]3.5L V6 VQ35DE engine[/b], the 350Z featured a [b]perfect 50/50 weight distribution[/b] and r[b]ear-wheel-drive layout[/b], making it an ideal platform for drifting and motorsports. Its performance even earned it a [b]Formula DRIFT Championship title[/b].

The [b]350Z’s aggressive styling[/b] took inspiration from its classic Z-car predecessors, blending retro heritage with a bold, modern look that remains iconic today.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/2348c1367e752e06bf023ac6585aa0d1b041ffbb.png[/img]

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

With [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] premiere just around the corner, we know you’re eager to see more of the cars we’ve prepared for you. Watch the showcase video and see these iconic Subaru cars in action:

[previewyoutube=PcVjpIOdPhQ;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Subaru Takes the Stage![/h3]
In [b]JDM[/b], you’ll have the freedom to choose from a range of legendary cars. We’ve handpicked a selection of [b]fan-favorite Subaru models[/b], including:
[list]
[*] [b]Subaru BRZ (2013)[/b] – one of the most balanced and engaging sports cars.
[*] [b]Subaru BRZ II (2022)[/b] – refined for the perfect driving experience.
[*] [b]Subaru Impreza WRX STI (2002)[/b] – rally icon with an unmistakable hood scoop, and raw performance.
[/list]… and more! While we won’t reveal everything just yet, get ready to drift, race, and push these machines to their limits. Keep reading to discover some fun facts about the showcased Subaru models!

[h3]Subaru BRZ[/h3]
The BRZ name comes from three key elements: [b]Boxer engine, Rear-wheel drive[/b], and Z, which symbolizes the car reaching its peak performance potential - [b]Zenith[/b]. Unlike many performance cars, the BRZ sticks to a [b]naturally aspirated 2.0L/2.4L boxer engine[/b], prioritizing [b]sharp throttle response and precision handling[/b] over raw power.

With its [b]rear-wheel-drive layout, well-balanced chassis, and ultra-low center of gravity[/b], the BRZ is a [b]favorite among drifters and track enthusiasts[/b], offering a playful yet controlled driving experience.

The BRZ’s simple yet effective design makes it a [b]dream platform for tuners[/b], with endless possibilities for [b]performance upgrades, widebody kits, and custom builds[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ff9729014b59866580e1bfa233b32d4f10469b80.png[/img]
[h3]Subaru BRZ II[/h3]
The [b]second-generation Subaru BRZ[/b], introduced in [b]2022[/b], takes everything fans loved about the original and refines it for an even better driving experience. Unlike its predecessor, the new BRZ features a [b]larger 2.4L naturally aspirated Boxer engine[/b], increasing both [b]horsepower and torque[/b], providing more low-end power for improved acceleration.

Subaru fine-tuned the [b]chassis and suspension[/b], making the car more rigid yet still playful, while maintaining its [b]signature low center of gravity[/b] for precise handling.

A [b]digital instrument cluster[/b] and an [b]upgraded infotainment system[/b] bring modern tech into the mix, while [b]Track Mode[/b] and [b]reworked stability control settings [/b]allow drivers to push the car’s limits with confidence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/34bdba69b1779a65635a57e46569302f795570b4.png[/img]
[h3]Subaru Impreza WRX STI[/h3]
Introduced in the 1990s, the Impreza quickly became a rally icon, dominating the [b]World Rally Championship (WRC)[/b] with its [b]turbocharged Boxer engine, all-wheel-drive system[/b], and aggressive aerodynamics. The [b]2002 WRX STI[/b] is often referred to as the "Bugeye" due to its round headlights.

This model also introduced the [b]Driver Controlled Center Differential (DCCD)[/b], allowing drivers to manually adjust torque distribution between the front and rear wheels.

Thanks to its [b]rally heritage, unmistakable hood scoop, and raw performance[/b], the WRX STI remains a dream car for JDM fans, tuners, and motorsport enthusiasts worldwide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/c23c962d9359a9e02c9754a1c5634d7679b80ef8.png[/img]

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

We're thrilled to bring some of [b]Mazda[/b]'s most iconic models to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]! We've already shown you the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/4349999161832006595]announcement of our collaboration[/url], but today we're taking it a step further - check out our latest showcase video to see these machines in all of their beauty!

[previewyoutube=MWDYH8GH0ig;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Drive Legendary Mazda Models[/h3]
In [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/url], you’ll be able to take the wheel of beautifully recreated Mazda legends, including:
[list]
[*][b] Mazda MX-5 (NA) | 1990[/b] - A lightweight car made for pure driving joy
[*] [b]Mazda RX-8 | 2005[/b] - A bold design and high-revving rotary engine
[*] [b]Mazda RX-7 FD | 1999[/b] - A drifting icon with timeless style and power
[/list]…and more that we won’t spoil now, so you have something to look forward to, when the game launches! We are, of course, still working on additional models! In the meantime, check out the interesting facts about the cars you can see in our video:

[h3]MAZDA MX-5 (NA)[/h3]
The Mazda MX-5 NA, the first-generation Miata, has been a symbol of driving joy for over 30 years. Debuting in 1989 (1990 in Europe), it redefined the sports car market with its [b]lightweight, agile, and affordable design[/b].

Built on the "[i]Jinba Ittai[/i]" philosophy—unity between driver and car—it delivers a pure driving experience with a [b]short-ratio manual transmission, a perfectly balanced chassis, and iconic pop-up headlights[/b].

Beloved in motorsport, from track racing to rallying, the Miata’s nimble handling and durability make it a top choice. Over the years, it has also become a pop culture icon, appearing in films, games, and music—a true legend on and off the road.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/03fa8de58a904d20b6898c25077ff1a75cda3ad6.png[/img]
[h3]MAZDA RX-7[/h3]
The Mazda RX-7 is one of the most iconic Japanese sports cars, known for its lightweight design, sleek styling, and revolutionary rotary engine. 

One of the RX-7’s biggest innovations came with the [b]third-generation[/b] [b]FD model (1992-2002)[/b], which featured the world’s first [b]mass-produced sequential twin-turbocharged engine[/b]. This system reduced turbo lag and provided smooth power delivery, making the FD RX-7 one of the best-handling cars of its era. 

Beyond the streets, the RX-7 gained fame in motorsports, including victories at the [b]24 Hours of Daytona[/b] and the [b]IMSA GT Championship[/b]. 

It also became a pop culture icon in films, anime, and video games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/bff681564636785411af9e4f0ec224a71817353a.png[/img]
[h3]MAZDA RX-8[/h3]
The Mazda RX-8, produced from [b]2003 to 2012[/b], was the spiritual successor to the legendary RX-7 and the final production car to feature Mazda’s iconic [b]Wankel rotary engine[/b].

One of the RX-8’s standout features was its [b]unique freestyle rear doors[/b], which provided easier access to the rear seats while maintaining a sleek coupe design. This made it a rare [b]four-seater sports car,[/b] blending practicality with performance.

It saw success in motorsports, competing in events like the [b]Super GT[/b] and [b]Nürburgring 24 Hours[/b], and became a staple in car culture through various racing video games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/23130091dd07e467c150f16c679477d52427fb51.png[/img]
To ensure authenticity, we’ve meticulously scanned each model, capturing every detail and ensuring they look, feel, and drive as they should. From body lines to handling characteristics, we’re bringing the true spirit of these JDM classics to life.

notes.title: JDM Gameplay Showcase
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] will officially hit the streets on [b]March 26th, 2025[/b], so today, we’re diving deep into the heart of our game. For both die-hard JDM enthusiasts and newcomers to the scene, our game is designed to be the ultimate tribute to Japanese car culture. Buckle up as we revisit the highlights and take a closer look at what you can expect!

[previewyoutube=-eamafuZQ3A;full][/previewyoutube]
When it comes to racing games, the way cars feel and behave on the road is the backbone of the experience. That’s why we’ve poured our hearts into creating a [b]simcade[/b] driving model that strikes the perfect balance between realism and accessibility.

[i][h2]Here’s what makes the JDM driving experience unique:[/h2][/i]
[h3]Simulation Backbone[/h3]
Our driving model is built on a fully simulated real-world physics foundation. This means cars have realistic weight and braking power - learning how to control acceleration and hand braking is key to cornering and mastering drifts.

In addition, dynamic weather effects like rain, fog, etc. will influence your car’s traction on the road. It is the same with detailed tuning options – suspension, drivetrain, engine power, and more. You can modify your car’s setup to suit your driving style and improve its performance.

[h3]Arcade Layers[/h3]
Once we were happy with the realism of the simulation, we added arcade elements to make the game approachable for everyone. 

Driving Assists will help you turn driving aids on or off, tailoring the experience to their skill level and playstyle. We’ve also prepared a driving school in game, which will help you gain essential skills and hone them; from grip racing to drifting. Whether you’re a casual player just looking for some fun or a dedicated drifter ready to master every corner, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] offers a tailored experience for everyone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/988fd5e3c0279f05e1f5d3346b0da8eaf22b045c.png[/img]
[h3]Get Ready for March 26th, 2025![/h3]

notes.title: Let’s say farewell to the Demo-Prologue!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

As the full version of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] approaches, big changes are on the horizon. The final round of [i]JDM Champions[/i] is here, but before we crown the last winners, it's time to bid farewell to the beloved prologue demo—[b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/url][/b].

With the release date announcement, you got a first look at the gameplay, captured directly from the latest build of the full version, and can see firsthand how the project has evolved since. We've put so much work into [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] that we feel the prologue-demo from August 2024 no longer represents the current state and quality of the game.

[previewyoutube=3gZDF4vnb_4;full][/previewyoutube]
We’ve gathered valuable feedback from [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/url][/b] players, which has been a key motivation in making the full version an even bigger and better experience for everyone. Here are a few key factors that led to our decision to close the prologue-demo.

[h3]Visual Fidelity[/h3]
We’ve updated the engine to [b]Unreal Engine 5[/b] significantly improving lighting, reflections, shadows, and overall visual quality. We’re working hard to eliminate ghosting and other visual issues, which were present in the demo. [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] will meet and exceed the visual standards of a 2025 release.

[h3]Unreal Engine 5[/h3]
Upgrading to UE5 has brought performance improvements and better game optimization, giving us more tools to fine-tune the experience for PC players. The process is still ongoing but the progress so far has been phenomenal. We’re committed to delivering a well-polished product on launch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/6a5274f17790df3fc378c72aa49842628186d863.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/b08c1456e249aa68cb553f36c203c141b897db99.png[/img]
[h3]Game Physics[/h3]
We’ve also refined the driving experience based on your valuable feedback. While driving physics can be subjective, we’ve focused on enhancing the overall feel of the cars on the road while expanding the functionality of driving assists. Our goal is to create the ultimate [b]simcade experience[/b]—a perfect balance where both sim-racing enthusiasts and casual players can enjoy a rewarding challenge and pure driving fun!

[h3]Binding System[/h3]
We've been testing steering wheels, pedals, shifters, and handbrakes from various manufacturers. From industry giants like Logitech G and Thrustmaster to lesser-known brands and generic controllers, our goal is to make as many devices as possible [b]plug-and-play[/b] at launch. At the same time, we're enhancing our [b]custom binding system[/b], ensuring that even if we miss a device, you'll still be able to race seamlessly.

With all the improvements we’ve made, demo-prologue [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/url][/b] no longer reflects the quality of the full game which will be a significantly enhanced experience in comparison. As a result, we’ll be shutting it down on Monday, [b]February 3rd at 3:00 p.m. CET,[/b] in preparation for the official launch of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] on [b]March 26th.[/b]

notes.title: Drifting Towards the Finish Line!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

The finish line is just a few laps away, and we’re beyond excited to share the big news: 

[h3]JDM: Japanese Drift Master is officially launching on  March 26th, 2025![/h3] 

Get ready, because Guntama is opening its roads, inviting you to feel the thrill that only the streets of Japan can offer!

[previewyoutube=3gZDF4vnb_4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]BUILD YOUR DREAM CAR[/h3]
From installing a new ECU to adding those over-the-top[i] bōsōzoku [/i]exhausts, tuning in [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] is a car buff’s dream come true. Customize every aspect of your vehicle, from performance upgrades to bold visual styles. Take to the roads in one of the licensed cars and make every ride special! Subaru, Mazda, and Nissan cars are already in the game and we’re tirelessly working to bring new manufacturers to our digital streets.

[h3]EXPLORE GUNTAMA [/h3]
Our map boasts [b]over 250 km of main roads[/b] and countless iconic landmarks for car enthusiasts and fans of Japanese culture alike. From the recreated Himeji Castle to our version of the legendary [b]Daikoku Parking Area[/b] – we’ve crafted a cohesive and stunning world, blending the most famous tourist landmarks with the hidden gems of Japanese car culture. Whether you’re a die-hard drift fan, a street racing enthusiast, or someone who just wants to cruise through the scenic roads of Japan, there’s always something for you to discover. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/04fbceb441fd25cd1bea97d0897923b93809f68b.png[/img]
[h3]GET TO KNOW THE STORY[/h3]
Discover the story of [b]Touma[/b], a Polish driver chasing his dream of becoming a recognized name on Japan’s street racing scene. With the support of his Japanese friends, he enters the high-stakes world of underground racing, only to face fierce rivals determined to block his rise to the top. Will Touma overcome the challenges and achieve greatness? 

In [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b], Touma’s story is brought to life through immersive in-game events and a stunning manga (Japanese-style comic) created by our talented in-house art team. Each event you participate in will be accompanied by beautifully illustrated pages that guide you through the unfolding narrative and set the stage for what’s to come. The story and gameplay intertwine seamlessly, creating a cohesive and dynamic narrative. The loop begins with manga sequences, then transitions into a racing event, and ends with open-world exploration, where the next narrative episode will be marked. Experience a story that combines heart-pounding racing with a rich and captivating tale!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/e7f4ddde212a1311261eab7b88b4a7eb70fbd72e.png[/img]
[h3]FUN FOR EVERY DRIVER[/h3]
[b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master [/b]is a [b]simcade racer[/b], combining realistic simulation mechanics with fun and accessible arcade elements. Every car in the game has a unique feel – from its weight to the way it handles corners and braking at high speeds. We’ve designed the driving physics to strike the perfect balance between realism and sheer driving fun.

For simulation enthusiasts, we’ve added presets for a variety of [b]steering wheels and sim-racing gear[/b] – and we’ll continue adding more! Our robust key-binding system will let you configure virtually any hardware setup, even if it’s not plug-and-play out of the box. And don’t worry if you’re playing on a controller or keyboard – we’ve ensured the game feels just as satisfying, no matter your setup.

[h3]POWERED BY UNREAL ENGINE 5[/h3]
We’re thrilled to announce that [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] is now running on [b]Unreal Engine 5[/b]! This engine upgrade allowed us to improve the general visual fidelity of the game, whilst improving the overall performance. Get ready to drift in stunning detail!

[h2]Welcome to Guntama Prefecture[/h2]

[b]Guntama[/b], is a fictional region crafted to combine iconic landmarks and architectural styles from across Japan. It blends the rural charm of prefectures like Gunma and Hokkaido with the wonders of areas like Saitama and Hakone. From passing a replica of Himeji Castle to driving along the twists and turns of scenic mountain roads, every corner of Guntama is designed to immerse you in the heart of Japan.

Fans of our demo-prologue, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url], will recognize [b]Haikama Lake[/b] and the serene countryside roads connecting it to [b]Kiko Town[/b]. These picturesque rural settings are just the beginning. The full version expands the map to include exciting new destinations.

[h2]Explore New Horizons[/h2]

Head south to [b]Ichikara[/b], Guntama’s largest city. This bustling urban hub dazzles with neon lights, towering skyscrapers, and sleek modern architecture—a perfect backdrop for showcasing your tuned-up rides. Drifters will also love [b]Daikotsu Parking Area[/b], inspired by Japan’s famous Daikoku PA, where you can hone your skills and show off your moves.

Our dedication to detail extends to each location's unique identity. For example, [b]Mount Natsuna[/b] pays homage to the legendary Mount Haruna, while [b]Chichira Bridge[/b] takes inspiration from the iconic Tatara Bridge, connecting players to even more exciting areas.

notes.title: Let’s Meet the JDM Cast!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

In the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/507318003732316229]last devlog[/url], we introduced you to the story of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] and showed our protagonist, [b]Tomasz "Touma" Stanowski[/b], who travels to Japan to fulfill his dream of a career as a drifter. Touma is not alone on his journey to the top. As you progress through the game, you will meet a diverse group of characters who bring their own goals and problems to the story and help the main character develop his skills and realize his dreams.

[h2]Meet the JDM: Japanese Drift Master cast![/h2]

[h3]Hideo Inoue[/h3]
Hideo, a friend Touma met through social media, works at Sakata's tuning shop. In a way, it is thanks to him that Touma decides to travel to the land of cherry blossoms. Once a talented racing driver, his career was cut short by a tragic accident that left him physically and emotionally scarred. Today, Hideo fulfills himself as a mechanic, building powerful machines and treating the success of the car he prepares as his own. He is Touma’s mentor in the world of tuning and the local racing scene, but he also proves that dreams can be realized in different ways.

[h3]Aoi Ishida[/h3]
Aoi, known from the prologue [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url], is the epitome of traditional Japanese values - charming, caring, and always ready to help. Her kindness and emotional support are invaluable during difficult moments in life, as well as on the track.

[h3]Keiko Tanaka[/h3]
Full of energy and always ready for the next adventure, Keiko works at the local sushi bar [i]Turbo Tuna House[/i], which she runs with her father. Keiko herself is a volcano of positive energy. She loves cosplay, anime, and feminine, cute cars - and her enthusiasm for the local motorsport scene as a fan and vlogger is contagious.

[h3]Kaori Kato[/h3]
An ambitious and independent artist, she owns a local paint shop where she creates stunning car veneer designs. She is also a drifter who is not afraid to challenge herself on the track. Kaori is a strong, confident woman who always speaks her mind and is an advocate for equality in her everyday life and in the world of street racing. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/e7f4ddde212a1311261eab7b88b4a7eb70fbd72e.png[/img]
[h2]Rivals on twisty roads[/h2]
The road to the top of the drifting world is no bed of roses, and Touma, who has no intention of relinquishing the title of best driver, will face dangerous rivals.

One of them is [b]Hatori “Scorpion” Hasashi[/b], seen in the prologue - a talented but arrogant rider who still can't get over having a new rival on the scene. Alongside him, you will also face [b]Dragon[/b], [b]Ayumi[/b], [b]Tiger[/b] and [b]Honey Badger[/b]. Friends, rivals, tuning, and drift - [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] has it all. With Touma's team and a host of unique opponents, you won't be bored for a second. Grab your steering wheel, gamepad or a keyboard, because there will be no shortage of excitement on the roads.

notes.title: Let's get to know the story!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

We want to start the New Year with a bang, so today we're taking you behind the scenes of the story that drives [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]. In our game, the narrative seamlessly intertwines with the gameplay, creating a harmonious and dynamic storytelling rhythm. The gameplay loop begins with manga sequences, followed by a story-driven event - a race - and then transitions back to open-world exploration with the next event location marked on the map. It all adds up to a rich and immersive experience.

While [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] is primarily a tribute to Japanese car culture, drifting and the challenges of winding mountain roads, it is also a story of dreams, struggles, and the search for a new beginning. Meet [b]Touma [/b]- the main protagonist who enters a world where drifting is not just a passion, but a way of life.

But before we dive into the story, we have prepared something special for you! Watch and feel the atmosphere that will soon be part of your experience.

[previewyoutube=kDFXd-Ujn2s;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]New beginning in Japan[/h2]
[b]Tomasz Stanowski[/b], known to everyone as [b]Touma[/b], is a young man from Poland who, after the tragic loss of his parents, decides to leave his past behind and start afresh. Driven by his childhood dream of becoming a drifter, he sets off for Japan - the birthplace of drifting on its winding mountain roads. He is greeted by Hideo, an online friend and tuning shop employee, who helps him navigate the local car scene.

During his first days in Japan, the ever-optimistic Touma meets [b]Keiko[/b] - an equally energetic girl who runs a local sushi bar with her father. It's there that Touma takes a job as a sushi delivery driver, roaming around the city in search of orders - and any opportunity to hone his driving skills. Every take-out, every turn of the wheel brings him one step closer to mastering the art of drifting and fulfilling his long-held dreams.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/54d35bd17a1b4963460a084f47f8a2e1d31eac68.png[/img]
[h2]Fighting for dreams[/h2]
It soon becomes clear that the road to the top won't be easy. Touma comes face to face with [b]Hatori “Scorpion” Hasashi[/b] - a character some of you may know from the demo prologue [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/url][/b]. This arrogant but exceptionally talented rival doesn't see Tomasz as a worthy opponent and doesn't hesitate to throw obstacles in his way. Their disdain for each other grows into a tense rivalry that fuels Touma's determination to fight for his dreams.

Will Tomasz be able to leave his troubled past behind and find his place in the drifting world? Will his move to Japan be the fulfillment of his dreams or just another disappointment? Find out the answers as you navigate the touges, highways, and towns of JDM: Japanese Drift Master.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8aa5938f43896ddaea5a1ace49026f61013be4f1.jpg[/img]
[h2]JDM premieres in spring 2025![/h2]
We can't wait for you to dive into this story and take your place in the starting line as Touma. Remember to add the game to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]wishlist[/url], hit the '[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]Follow[/url]' button on Steam, and keep an eye out on our [url=https://linktr.ee/japanesedriftmaster]social media[/url] - more updates will be coming your way soon! notes.title: Let’s Build a JDM Car!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

In Gaming Factory, cars are our life. Not only do we drive around[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/4451340938215687395]racetracks[/url]to learn all about drifting, but we also privately work on our own vehicles.

This year, we visited Gamescom in Cologne, Germany, and brought an RX-7 with us. The car wasn’t a rental—it belongs to one of our developers, [b][url=https://www.instagram.com/__bananaboy__?igsh=dDg3cTg1NmZsZjBl&utm_source=qr]BananaBoy[/url][/b]. The Mazda has become something of a star at the show, so we thought we’d share a bit of its background with you. To do that, we interviewed the owner. Let’s get started!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/250b55f285f753bc8f2e2115d85c443bf41de55c.png[/img]
[h3]Why did you choose this particular model?[/h3]

The Mazda RX-7 has always been on my ‘must-have’ list of cars—it’s my absolute favorite JDM in terms of looks. In 2016, I made a 500-kilometer drive across Poland to trade my Subaru for an RX-7. However, I ended up backing out because the poor condition of the Mazda didn’t compare to the pristine Impreza I had. For the next six years, I regretted that decision! 😊

[h3]Does your car have a unique history or an interesting past?[/h3]

Is it interesting? That’s not for me to judge. Unfortunately, many of today’s highly sought-after JDMs have a similar story, often without a happy ending. This particular RX-7 comes from Japan, where it was driven from 1993 for at least ten years. It later made its way to the UK, where it underwent numerous mechanical modifications. When it was imported to Poland in 2012, it had a freshly built engine with around 500 horsepower. Interestingly, the car was imported with the intention of removing the engine and other parts, which were repurposed into another RX-7. Since then, it had been sitting in a corner of a garage, gathering dust.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/fb2bb874e6affb0c3a725fbec24e433375887a33.png[/img]
[h3]Was this car difficult to acquire? What was the buying process like?[/h3]

The Mazda RX-7 is a 30-plus-year-old legend that still commands a high price. In the spring of 2022, I decided it was now or never. I spread the word among friends in the industry and on motoring groups, searching for an RX-7—whether it was a project, a rebuild, or a model in great condition. A few offers came through, including the car we’re discussing today. However, because it was incomplete, I initially opted for a fully operational Mazda. A few months later, the same car turned up again, this time at a much better price. Even though I already owned one RX-7, I simply couldn’t say no!

[h3]What key modifications did you make and why?[/h3]

A more accurate question might be, “Is there anything you haven’t modified?” 😛 As I mentioned, the car had been collecting dust in the shop for about ten years without an engine. During that time, it had been “robbed” of parts needed for other projects. By the time I bought it back, you could say it was just a bare shell with no drivetrain and a rundown interior. The car essentially needed to be built from scratch. It was completely rebuilt, both mechanically and visually, and now sports a new color as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/6cb5d6e63f7da32d7686885a1c5d589a78b842a4.png[/img]
[h3]Do you have any plans for future improvements or tuning?[/h3]

Of course! As of today, I still consider the car unfinished, and it needs additional work. First, the electrics need to be completed—I want the car to be fully functional, which includes working air conditioning, gauges, and a sound system. The suspension also needs attention. I plan to replace the stock control arms with adjustable ones, radically alter the geometry for drifting, and possibly upgrade the wheels to something more interesting.

[h3]What engine is in your car? How much power does your car's engine generate and what vehicle performance it assures?[/h3]

The current engine is the complete opposite of the original rotary (Wankel) engine—a 3-liter M57 diesel from BMW. So, I swapped out a high-revving, low-torque petrol engine for a slow-revving diesel with several times the torque. At this stage, after the engine swap, it produces 260 horsepower and about 600 Nm of torque. This is more than enough for drifting. However, if I decide I need more power, this engine has the potential to handle significant upgrades comfortably.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/7d7f584bde50b7cf25a97b8eb78ec7e8483b01fa.png[/img]
[h3]What is your favourite visual element on your car? (e.g. body kit, paint job, wheels).[/h3]

I don’t think I have a single favorite component. For me, the most important thing is how the individual parts come together to form a cohesive whole. The body kit from C-West, combined with the RE Amemiya bonnet and carbon wing, is my favorite tuning "package" for the RX-7 body. The car has beautiful lines on its own, and these additions guarantee it catches the eye of anyone with even a passing interest in cars. I didn’t want to overwhelm those lines with a flashy color. The factory red was replaced with Titanium Gray, also from the Mazda RX-7 factory palette, and subtly enhanced with a wraparound livery reminiscent of the early 2000s—the golden age of tuning in Japan and worldwide. I’ve paired the look with classic sports rims, the Work Emotion 11R. However, I wouldn’t rule out switching to something else in the future. I tend to get bored quickly and like to change things up. 😊 

[h3]Is your exhaust system custom? If so, what did you change and why?[/h3]

The entire exhaust system is handmade from stainless steel. Since it’s a supercharged diesel, it doesn’t produce enough noise to require mufflers. As a result, it’s a straight pipe with a 3-inch diameter, expanding to 4.5 inches in the end section.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3bf3af07de90592288506eb62eef7b2bc0b3677f.png[/img]
[h3]What makes this car unique from other JDM cars?[/h3]

(Wankel) engine was also a signature feature of the RX series, and no other widely known JDM model had a similar engine. Now, with the diesel swap, it’s even more distinctive. I haven’t come across another RX-7 FD anywhere in the world where someone has made a modification quite like this—it’s a bit of a controversial choice! 😛

[h3]How do people react when they see your car on the street?[/h3]

The hype around Japanese classics has grown enormously in recent years. I often see people taking photos of my car, pointing at it, or hearing children shout in excitement. You have to realize that these cars are almost extinct—there are only a few dozen left in Poland. In my town, only two RX-7s have been spotted over the last decade, and both of them are mine. This makes the car very special. For my generation, the RX-7 is an icon, well-known from games and films. Seeing one in person on the street becomes a memorable experience, even for those who don’t consider themselves car enthusiasts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/4edae82d1bcdb3e21ff9e02a05e0492392cf0ce7.png[/img]
[h3]Do you own any other cars? If so, do you have any favourites?[/h3]

There are plenty of cars I’d like to own, but my budget doesn’t allow me to have them all at once, so I change cars frequently—selling and buying as I go. I bought my first car in 2011, and since then, I’ve owned about 200 different models. If that sounds absurd, just imagine my friend, who owns a similar number of cars at any given time, spread across different storage locations. 😊 Currently, I own the RX-7 we’ve been discussing, a Nissan 350Z, a Volkswagen Golf Convertible (my first car), a Lincoln Limousine from one of Donald Trump’s hotels, a Peugeot 206 RC, and a Tesla Model S, which is my daily driver. Over the years, I’ve also had many radically different vehicles, including around 20 Mazda MX-5s, a Hummer H2, a Porsche Boxster, 911, and Cayenne, a Bentley Continental GT, an Aston Martin DB9, three Nissan Silvia S15s, two Skyline R34s, a Toyota Chaser, two Subaru Impreza WRXs, an original Mazda RX-7, and many more.

Right now, I’m saving up for my next dream car—a Ferrari or Lamborghini.

Thank you for the talk!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/44262b989cdfebdfcf1aed3578e930ccc1afd257.png[/img]

We hope this interview has given you a closer look at what it means to own and cherish a piece of JDM history. If you have any burning questions or your own stories about your dream cars, let us know in the comment section below!

Don't forget to add [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] to your Steam [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]wishlist[/url] and push the “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]Follow[/url]” button to receive the latest updates. Also join our amazing community on [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] where the discussion never ends. See you on the track!

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Today, we’re taking you on a high-octane journey that bridges the gap between real-life racing action and the immersive virtual world of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]. [h3]Introducing the JDM x Racing Tracks Showcase [/h3]
To develop the best racing game possible we need to understand racing at its core. To do that we show up at various events, focusing our attention on drifting challenges. This year we had the pleasure to participate in [url=https://www.facebook.com/japfestpl?locale=pl_PL][b]Japfest[/b][/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/JDM3M?locale=pl_PL][b]JDM Trójmiasto[/b][/url] events, here in Poland. To share a little bit of fun we had with you folks, we’ve put together a special video combining footage from real-life racing events and runs in our game. From the roar of engines to the squeal of tires. It’s a true celebration of the passion and artistry of drifting, both in real life and in the virtual world.

[previewyoutube=tb9f2oNq9a8;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]This epic crossover wouldn’t have been possible without the incredible events that fueled our inspiration: [/i]

[h3]Japfest[/h3]
At Japfest, one of the biggest celebrations of Japanese car culture in Europe, attendees had the chance to not only witness stunning drift car parades and custom-tuned beauties but also dive into the world of JDM with on-site driving simulators provided by [b]Simracing School[/b]! Equipped with full steering wheel setups, fans could test their skills in JDM: Japanese Drift Master while competing for exclusive prizes.

[h3]JDMTrójmiasto[/h3]
In Tricity, Poland, the JDM Community event brought together fans, drivers, and gamers alike. The picturesque Polish coast provided the perfect backdrop for filming live-action content that you saw in today’s showcase. This event captured the essence of car culture and the camaraderie that comes with it. The feedback we received from the community was incredible.

Participating in drift events allowed us to recreate the spirit of these events in JDM: Japanese Drift Master. We wanted to ensure that every turn of the track, every detail of the scenery, and every drift you do in the game reflected the thrill of being on the track in person.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/cad50244dffe1a9dc5552a1b1938f2fbfb686e23.png[/img]

notes.title: Production Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

As the year comes to a close, we wanted to provide a small summary of what you might expect in the full version of the game, which will be released in [b]Spring 2025[/b].

Your feedback, comments, and DMs since the launch of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] was an immense help to our development process. We hear what you are saying and we know there’s still a lot we can improve before the game releases. To highlight a few aspects that are at the top of our priorities:
[list]
[*] [b]Performance[/b] - our goal is to have the game running smoothly even on weaker GPUs or perform better on mid and high end GPUs. We’re actively improving game streaming, as well as lighting, shadows and… well basically all aspects of the game, so you can enjoy [b]JDM[/b] on the PCs you already own. 

[*] [b]Input devices[/b] - steering wheels, pedal panels, handbrakes and shifters - we’re systematically adding support for additional devices and testing them in-house to be sure everything is ready for launch. That includes hardware dedicated strictly for sim racers, as well as mainstream devices you can find in electronic stores across the globe and even cheap stuff you can get online with little to no branding on them. Of course, we won’t be able to cover every single device available out there and check every single combination of devices, e.g. Logitech steering wheel, paired up with a Thrustmaster handbrake and a Moza shifter, so our robust key binding system will make a reappearance. It will be updated and will contain more settings so that with a little bit of time you will be able to bind anything to play[b] JDM[/b] with. 
[/list]
[h2]Story[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/08b706515ef7cf92bb1bc9b845b7d9216ecea17e.png[/img]
Racing games rarely have an engaging plotline assigned to them. With a game inspired by Japan and its culture, it felt almost obligatory to implement manga into the gameplay. And so we did! With a full team of manga artists in-house we’re drawing the story page by page, all of which will tie to every single story event that you will encounter in the game. 

Each story event will push the manga forward and at any time you will be able to read the unlocked pages via your smartphone, a feature you could already see in our prologue-demo [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/url][/b].

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] introduced a prequel story to the game, which you won’t find in the full game. It’s set a few years earlier and introduces some important characters that will shape the story of JDM. The prologue is free to play, so if you haven’t done so already, you might want to check it out. 

Our fictional prefecture - Guntama - will see a lot of racing very soon. You will meet colorful characters, some of them will become your friends, others fierce rivals. Expect a lot of action, drama and even some romance. We’ll get back to you with more details, early next year!

[h2]Open World [/h2]

When we started the development of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] we had one goal in mind - recreating Japan as precisely as it was possible. Starting with the architecture and surrounding nature and ending with the roads you will drive on. Let’s stop here for a second and talk about the latter.

If you’ve played enough racing games in your life, you might have noticed that they place you either on racing tracks or city streets where every road is as wide as a highway. Japan is known for its narrow, winding passes, extremely tight streets and even more extreme mountain corners, so this approach just wouldn’t cut it. Aiming for credibility, we wanted to recreate Japan roads as they are in reality, adding additional layers of experience to the game - one of authenticity so that roaming around our fictional Guntama feels like the real deal and one of gameplay complexity. In JDM you just won’t be able to go 200 miles per hour at all times - controlling your speed, the gear you're in and when you need to break will be as crucial as learning and understanding drifting (to cut those corners faster). We believe our game is the only title out there that provides such an experience. 

Of course, we are continually working on expanding the Guntama prefecture, populating it with various, recognizable landmarks and architecture. Some are generally known to the global populace, some will have a deeper meaning for automotive fans - legendary car spots will find their way into JDM! Stay tuned next year for more precise information on the subject. For now, take a look at some examples from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url].

The [i]Machi-no-Eki Yusuhara[/i] building might not be a hotel in-game, but it’s still a recognizable landmark, whose purpose has been tied to the story and mood aspects of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/97499041f05394e6f24553eb599f1857215ebeea.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/de69c4e7595da3abdde9aafeff7092e166e6bacd.png[/img]

[i]Haruna Lake[/i] is called [i]Haikama Lake [/i]in JDM. See and decide for yourselves if we gave justice to this location.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/e706f33e760d68d137c663be7f044b34d9e01d90.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/37a20423c85dbcdf85b4de2b559b2412ba044b2a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/96448d7528b7f2b628b3fa3ae335f9f8fbb16a26.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/68c5583d3de2b0738d7125519aa75609f8cfa462.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/746086fb83344fd9ffee3e93eb827e565ee44476.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/190a6eab7f05b7bbc77921e6e52e4f81f2a93c04.png[/img]
Throughout the development of JDM, we strived to bring characteristic Japanese landmarks to the game and the examples above only scratch the surface of the content you will be able to uncover, as you drive around Guntama. If you’re a Japanese resident or a frequent tourist you will definitely recognise some spots. If you haven’t done so already, launch JDM: ROTS and see how many references you can find and let us know in the comments! :) 

[h2]Tuning[/h2]
Before we close this devlog, let us say a few words about tuning, as it’s one of the most frequent subjects you ask about. It’s happening and growing by the day, both in terms of visual and technical tuning. Speaking of the latter - you will be able to buy new parts for each car. Those parts will come in tiers - each tier more expensive, but providing better performance. For as long as you can afford it, you can buy any part you want. On top of that, more advanced parts will unlock the ability to fine-tune your car's performance. We’re not ready to go into details, but expect an update focused on the subject next year.

And as for visual tuning, let the images speak for themselves:

[previewyoutube=7Y-Xjd5fyXw;full][/previewyoutube]
Again, we will share more details on visual tuning with you next year.

That’s it for today. We hope you enjoyed this little summary. Tell us in the comments what made you interested in JDM in the first place. Also, don’t forget to  📌 Hit ‘Follow’ on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]Steam page[/url] and add [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] to your wishlist to stay up-to-date on all announcements.

To be eligible for the competition, you must:
[list]
[*] Create a graphic design of your Mural in [b]3840x3840 px resolution[/b] in [b]PNG format with no background[/b], using an [b]RGBA color palette[/b]. It can be texts, pictures, drawings, doodles, or a mix of all of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/221c74a6eb360d0ae39a31658059797d4b4e06d3.png[/img]

notes.title: Let’s Answer!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

It’s time for another [b]Q&A session[/b]! The development of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] has come a long way, and we know you’ve got plenty of questions that need answers. A lot has changed since the demo version, so consider this devlog your most up-to-date source of information.

We’re thrilled by your curiosity, and while some answers will have to wait, we promise there’s a lot to look forward to. With the premiere getting closer, plenty of surprises and reveals are lined up in the months ahead. Don’t miss a beat—join the [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]JDM Discord[/url] and follow our [url=https://linktr.ee/japanesedriftmaster]social media[/url] for all the latest updates!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/50f3d1a87931f927805df0c59412164cb9d0e72c.png[/img]

We’ve compiled the most frequently asked questions from the community into one place just for you—check it out!

[b]Q. When will there be a JDM launch?
A. [/b]The game is scheduled to be released in Spring 2025.

[b]Q. Will JDM be available for consoles?
A. [/b]At the moment our main focus is on the PC version. For the console release information follow our announcements.

[b]Q. Is it possible to leave the car and move on foot across the map?
A. [/b]No. It’s a car driving game only. As much as we would want to provide you with an option to walk around Guntama, it would steer our attention away from what’s really important here - drifting in beautiful cars at scenic Japanese vistas.

[b]Q. How can we get a free key to the game?
A. [/b]We’re not offering free keys to the game per say, but we occasionally host various contests in which you can win a key. Follow our social media and join our Discord to never miss your chance to win one.  Join the fun! ➡️ [url=https://linktr.ee/japanesedriftmaster]JDM LINKTREE[/url]  

[b]Q. Is there a YouTube or Spotify playlist with music in JDM?
A. [/b]We have a playlist available on Spotify. It’s not a full JDM OST yet, but we promise to build it up for launch! ➡️ [url=https://open.spotify.com/playlist/7ErhMg9jw0dcjcmXo7XC73?si=4145127845e24a2b ]JDM PLAYLIST[/url] 

[b]Q. Will there be DLC or updates after the release?
A. [/b]Yes, the initial release is only the beginning for JDM. Expect content updates after release. We will share more details closer to the game's launch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/01083520f07d28a0a45e5426e4da1c34fa6268dd.png[/img]

[b]Q. Will there be optimization for Steam Deck?
A. [/b]Optimization of the game is extremely important to us, we are constantly working to make our game as accessible as possible for everyone. At this point, we can't promise that yet, because we are still in the production phase, but we will certainly let our players know everything before the release.

[b]Q. Will the players be able to modify the drift physics of the cars? 
A. [/b]Of course! There will be a robust tuning system in place, where you will be able to tune your car to any needs, be it drift, grip, or even drag. Expect more detailed info on the subject next year.

[b]Q. Is JDM: Rise of the Scorpion and JDM demo the same thing?
A. [/b]Yes they are. JDM: Rise of the Scorpion launched as a separate store product, but has been moved since to the main JDM: Japanese Drift Master store page as a demo to avoid player confusion.

[b]Q. Is there a list of steering wheels supported by the game?
A. [/b]Not at this time. However, we’ve seen and taken to heart all of your feedback and hardware requests from the JDM: Rise of the Scorpion. We are working on the new binding system and we’re continually adding new devices to the game. We want as many devices as humanly possible to work for the launch of JDM. 

[b]Q. Will there be a possibility to set a point wherever you want on the map (to guide you to the place)?
A. [/b]Yes, you will be able to mark a spot through an in-game GPS system that will find you the route to your destination, making it easier for you to navigate our open world.
 
[b]Q. Maybe it's confidential, but will the map be fully explorable, or will you have to unlock the regions one by one?
A. [/b]The map will be fully explorable from the beginning. The moment you hit play, you will be able to drive to any of our beautiful landmarks and soak in the Japanese road atmosphere. Note that story events will unlock with your progression and will need to be completed before the next unlocks and becomes visible on your map. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/72ffd088cfe88c938f588d70c539509c4619805a.png[/img]

Want to dive deeper into the production process or share your ideas? Write down your questions as comments to this devlog. We might not answer them immediately, but they will serve as a basis for the next Q&A round. For a more engaging discussion, join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord server[/url] to connect with the community and the JDM team directly! If you never want to miss a beat about all the latest JDM news, be sure to hit that [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Follow button[/b][/url] on the game’s main Steam Page! Don’t forget to follow us on [url=https://linktr.ee/japanesedriftmaster]social media[/url] and, if you haven’t done so already, be sure to add [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b] to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/]Steam wishlist[/url].

We know you’ve been itching to get your hands on the full release of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] and we’re pleased to say we have a release window set!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/82df84ebe79aaa0ed4013d3f208335730be9ce5c.png[/img]
With all of the feedback we have received from you after the release of the demo-prologue [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] and the countless hours we spent talking to you on various events throughout the year, we dove deep into polishing the details and improving the overall quality of the game, so you can get the best possible experience on day one.

We thank you for your patience and believe us when we say that we are as excited for the launch as you are, or even more. Continue reading for some additional information on what you can expect from the final release.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/

Let’s begin with the new trailer for [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b], giving you a sneak peek into the new location – [b]Ichikara[/b], which you will find in the full version of the game. This lively metropolis, inspired by Tokyo’s most modern districts, is packed with neon lights, towering billboards, and stunning skyscrapers that truly come alive both day and night. With references to legendary movie locations and spots treasured by drift and car enthusiasts, Ichikara offers an unforgettable atmosphere for racers and fans alike. 

Mark your calendars for the first quarter of next year and experience the thrill of Japanese street racing like never before. 

[h3]Watch the trailer now:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=vMnP89CHeZI;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]What awaits you in the full version of the game?[/h3]

[*] [b]Unique story[/b]: Immerse yourself in an engaging narrative presented through hand-drawn manga pages and follow the story of a foreign driver trying to make a name for himself on the streets of Japan. Over 40 story-oriented challenges await you, alongside dozens more side quests that will keep you immersed in the world of JDM.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/5be2d5480171e76538ad222726c1ef78f1a99b64.png[/img]
[*] [b]Huge world[/b]: Explore a vast, open world, created from real-life locations scattered across Japan and mixed to create our fictional prefecture - Guntama - a true paradise for drift racing. With over 250 kilometers of main roads, featuring scenic vistas, challenging mountain passes, bustling city streets, and serene rural areas, you will have plenty of spots to hone your driving skills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/a84ad85b1a0c1f0d988eb7bde28c1c617900e43a.png[/img]
[*] [b]Licensed cars[/b]: Get behind the wheel of fully licensed cars from renowned brands like Nissan, Subaru, or Mazda. Each of the cars was fully scanned and meticulously modeled, and their engine sounds were recorded—all for an authentic and immersive driving experience. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/03a0afef92c5dac8493170d447ed4053328973f5.png[/img]
[*] [b]Advanced tuning options[/b]: Customize and fine-tune your cars with a wide range of tuning options, from modifying car parts, to visual mods, unique paint jobs and even full mod kits, allowing for a truly personalized racing experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f908a2855c80ffa3a2632ee2d77b4e8eed5d2098.png[/img]
[*] [b]Variety racing events[/b]: Experience a diverse range of racing events that test your skills. From high-speed circuit races and intense drift challenges to time trials and special head-to-head battles and drag showdowns. Each event offers unique gameplay dynamics and opportunities to showcase your mastery behind the wheel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3eed83ef91bb0a510b36207f1584e020603ed603.png[/img]
We are working hard to deliver the best game possible to all of you, and we truly appreciate your feedback, understanding and support. In the meantime, you can immerse yourself in the world of JDM by playing our free prologue, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url]. notes.title: JDM: Rise of the Scorpion Content Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

Over the past few weeks, we've been hard at work preparing the latest major update for the free prologue, [b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b]. In this devlog, we’ll walk you through the new fixes, features, and some exciting upcoming news.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/496badcc331fa31820e545a92798ff1c42c67648.png[/img]

One of the key updates was transitioning [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] to the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] Steam page, where it will remain available as a free-to-play prologue-demo.

[h2]Now, let's dive into the details of the changes included in the latest update:[/h2]

[h3]Additions:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Online Leaderboards in Challenge Mode[/b]. Both the grip and drift challenges will have their own active Leaderboards. The players will see them after a finished race, or they can be accessed anytime from the Challenge Menu > Leaderboards. On the leaderboard tables, you will be able to check various stats for the score, including what car was used and what assists were turned on. It’s time to show who is the real king of Guntama streets!
[*] [b]Three new cars were added to the Challenge Mode[/b]. All of them have been mechanically and visually tuned for the occasion:
- Mazda RX8,
- Mazda MX-5 (NA),
- Subaru BRZ II.
[*] Added a new input preset for the Moza R5 Steering Wheel.
[*] Added HGP Shifter and HBP Handbrake to supported devices.
[/list][b]Check out the teaser introducing new car models now available in Challenge Mode:[/b]

[previewyoutube=noQtYN579nk;full][/previewyoutube][h3]Fixes:[/h3]
