notes.title: Let's Summarize the Prologue!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

We've made a small update to the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] Steam page! The free-to-play prologue, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url], is now available in the [b]demo section[/b]. This update provides a more unified experience, making it easier for you to access the game and any other JDM information directly from one place.

If you’ve missed the premiere of JDM: Rise of the Scorpion, below you will find a rundown of what to expect from our Prologue-Demo. 

[previewyoutube=LiOvNSu4A0w;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]MANGA AND STORY[/h3]
This free-to-play prologue is a unique introduction to the narrative of [b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b]. Meet Hatori Hasashi, an exemplary student from a traditional Japanese family, now determined to make a name for himself on the racetrack. Follow his rise to become the feared ‘Scorpion’ as he faces off against a variety of tough rivals.

Immerse yourself in a racing game that emphasizes story-driven gameplay with a unique narrative style. Instead of traditional cutscenes, the story comes to life through manga pages, offering a fresh way to experience the narrative. Characters and places portrayed in [b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b] will return in the full version of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/008753caa233a2f493fea9d46a2bbccd918ed20b.png[/img]
[h3]LICENSED CARS[/h3]
Gradually upgrade Hatori’s car and make it as fast and fierce as a scorpion’s strike. Experiment with different modifications, then put its performance to the test by racing through tight city streets and winding mountain passes against other skilled drivers.

Additionally, you’ll have the chance to test drive different cars, accessible after visiting the dealership from the open world, such as licensed [i]Nissan[/i], [i]Subaru[/i], and [i]Mazda[/i] models.

[h3]EVENTS + CHALLENGE MODE[/h3]
In [b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b], you’ll take on a variety of story-driven events and quests designed to push your driving skills to the limit. Whether it’s [b]drift races[/b], [b]grip challenges[/b], or intense [b]drift battles[/b], you’ll face off against tough competitors and prove your skills on the road.

If you want to test different car models on closed tracks try out the newly added single-player [b]Challenge Mode[/b]. Choose from stock vehicles or fine-tuned models for specific challenges. Whether you're chasing the best drift score or racing to be the fastest, this mode pushes your skills to the limit with [b]Drift[/b] and [b]Grip challenges[/b]. Face off against AI rivals, and continue refining your driving abilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/62b86e1cc9095d824d30acb7e344a5d94891b24b.png[/img]
[h3]LOCATIONS[/h3]
The story of [b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b] takes players to the fictional Japanese prefecture of Guntama - a place inspired and re-created from real-world locations. This area is filled with challenging roads, perfect for mastering your drifting techniques. Explore the scenic Tengai Forest and cruise through Kiko Town, where the heart of the story unfolds.

[b]The dynamic weather system[/b] introduces an unpredictable element to the racing experience, and with the[b] cycle of day and night[/b], every ride becomes unique. Whether you're drifting under the cover of darkness with the glow of local shop lights or at sunrise, each moment presents a different challenge and adventure.

[h3]SUPPORT AND TIPS[/h3]
We've put together a guide with solutions for the most common issues. Take a look to see if you can find a fix for the problem you're experiencing. If not, feel free to reach out to us via email at [i]support@jdmgame.com[/i] or join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] server to report bugs and issues through the dedicated channels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/c9a53e25b0be7bfc5cf85e2d0bb7383dba1f9cfd.png[/img]
[h3][b]DRIVING ASSISTS:[/b][/h3]
Since the demo, we’ve expanded the amount of driving assist options available to you. Some of them are now disabled when launching the game for the first time, so we’ve put together some essential information on what they do and what we recommend. While certain parameters may seem complex, our goal is to help you fine-tune your experience to best suit your style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/2d8ecdcddbae702171557d96012a9bea4f66c810.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]ABS[/b] - Enhances braking and helps to maintain control during turns. Recommended to keep ‘ON’ for improved driving stability.
[*] [b]TCS[/b] - Prevents wheel skidding. Turn ‘OFF’ when drifting for better skid control.
[*] [b]ESP[/b] - Helps to prevent loss of vehicle control. Recommended ‘OFF’ unless you’re roaming the open world or in situations where you want the car to keep steady on the track at all costs.
[*] [b]Gearbox [/b]- Adjusts the gearbox control type. Modify according to your driving preference.
[*] [b]Gamepad & Keyboard assist[/b] - Limits the car’s front axle twisting, making it easier to control via gamepad and keyboard. Turn ‘ON’ for gamepads and keyboard, and ‘OFF’ when using a steering wheel.
[/list]
[h3][b]CRASHES:[/b][/h3]
If you get an error on launch, in which OPENXR is mentioned, please do the following: remove the openxr_loader.dll file

You can find the file in the following folder: ProgramFiles(x86) > Steam > SteamApps > Common > JDMrots > Engine > Binaries > ThirdParty > OpenXR

[h3][b]PERFORMANCE ISSUES:[/b][/h3]
We're looking into performance issues some of you have been reporting; If you meet the game's requirements and experience low performance, please reach out to us at:[b] support@jdmgame.com[/b]. In the email please provide more information on your hardware specs, information on your in-game graphical settings, and information if the issues persist at all times or are only present in certain situations or locations. Also, please include a dxdiag file.

How to obtain a dxdiag file:
[list]
[*] Press the windows button on your keyboard
[*] Type dxdiag and hit enter
[*] Wait for the diagnostic tool to gather data and press save all information
[*] Attach the created .txt file to the email
[/list]
We need as much information as possible to understand where the issue is coming from and create a fix.

[h3][b]STUTTERING ISSUE:[/b][/h3]
We are aware of an issue where some AMD CPUs (most observed in the 5000 series) have a stuttering issue in JDM, which is caused by their PBO (Precision Boost Overdrive) function. If you use such a CPU, and you're experiencing frame stuttering/lag - turning that function off could help reduce or even get rid of the problem entirely.

If you're using AMD Adrenalin software you should turn off this function from automatically triggering, and additionally, you can also turn it off in BIOS:

To turn it off.
BIOS: Settings --> AMD OverClocking --> Precision Boost Overdrive

We’re actively working on a solution to this issue, but it may take more time to resolve it. Thank you for your understanding and patience as we sort it out. 

[h3][b]STEERING WHEEL SETTINGS:[/b][/h3]
We added presets for various steering wheels including Fanatec V2, Logitech G29, Logitech G920, Thrustmaster T150, Thrustmaster T300, and Thrustmaster T500.

Go to Settings > Control > Steering wheel > Choose the preset.

If you have different gear at home do not fret - we have you covered. You can custom bind almost anything through our custom binding feature. We’ve prepared a short video tutorial on how to customize keybindings for your hardware. Please watch it if you’re having trouble setting up your steering wheel.

We need as much information as possible to understand where the issue is coming from and create a fix.

[h2]STUTTERING ISSUE[/h2]
Our observations show some AMD CPUs (most observed in the 5000 series) have a stuttering issue in JDM, which is caused by their PBO (Precision Boost Overdrive) function. If you use such a CPU, and you're experiencing frame stuttering/lag - turning that function off could help reduce or even get rid of the problem entirely.

If you're using AMD Adrenalin software you should turn off this function from automatically triggering, and additionally, you can also turn it off in BIOS:

To turn it off.
BIOS: Settings --> AMD OverClocking --> Precision Boost Overdrive
[h2]STEERING WHEEL SETTINGS[/h2]
We’ve also prepared a short video tutorial on how to customize keybindings for your hardware. Please watch it if you’re having trouble setting up your steering wheel.

[previewyoutube=rzMybda8tog;full][/previewyoutube]
If you continue to experience issues after customizing keybindings, please send us your Saved/Config folder.

You can find this folder here: Main computer > System > Users > USER > AppData > Local > JDM > Saved > Config 

Email the folder to: [b]support@jdmgame.com[/b].

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

We are excited to announce that the standalone prologue to[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] - [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] - is now available! This is a special moment that we have been looking forward to for months.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/

[h3]We have prepared a premiere trailer for you, which gives a taste of what awaits you in the prologue. We encourage you to check it out:[/h3]

[previewyoutube=LiOvNSu4A0w;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Licensed cars[/h2]
Right now in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] you can get behind the wheel of licensed vehicles from brands Subaru and Mazda. Check out their performance and experience the thrills these iconic cars have to offer! Experience an amazing story with Hatori and his fast as scorpion's attack car, and check various vehicles on the test track.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/9b9568df94c52d704cd3a07b7b19e8938ef41fba.png[/img]
[h2]Exciting new events[/h2]
Face AI opponents in a variety of competitions that have their own unique story and purpose. Each race, is not only an opportunity to challenge your skills, but also an immersive narrative that gives the race a deeper meaning. Below you will find just some of the events we have prepared for you.

[h3]Drift Race [/h3]
Score as many points as possible by drifting through challenging corners.
[list]
[*] [b]Race with Ayumi[/b] - challenge your rich friend, who is known for her style and precision, by scoring more drift points than her. Push your limits, demonstrate perfect car control and leave Ayumi far behind.
[*] [b]Touge friends[/b] - Compete with your friends in rides where precision, technique and style count. Earn drift points on the twisty mountain tracks of Touge as you show off your skills and car control.
[/list][h3]Grip Race [/h3]
Speed up and be the first to cross the finish line.
[list]
[*] [b]Race against Satoru[/b] - Challenge your greatest rival and be the first to reach the finish line. This race is not only a matter of honour, but also a battle to maintain the good reputation of the Hasashi family. 
[*] [b]Race for a date[/b]- Outperform your rival to win the heart of Aoi. You must show your skills to the highest level, be fast, decisive and indefectible. Remember, what's at stake is not only winning the race, but also the chance of a special date with the special girl.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/0f83000f90b711f0a690d58cf70e81b706e0e334.png[/img]
[h2]Storyline and characters[/h2]
The plot of JDM: Japanese Drift Master is set in the fictional Japanese prefecture of Guntama. The area is inspired by the mountainous region of Honshu. If you are familiar with Japan's famous drifting tracks, you will find many similarities to the real world. 

The story presented through manga (a Japanese comic book), portrays the story of Hatori Hasashi and his path to becoming the titular 'Scorpion'. This model student and son of a traditional Japanese family takes his pride and arrogance to the race track, where various rivals await him. In addition to Hatori, players will meet a number of side characters who will play an important role during Scorpion's rising:
[list]
[*] [b]Aoi Ishida [/b]is a girl from a traditional family who has known Hatori since they were children. When they start dating, she supports him in every way she can, especially on the track.
[*] [b]Ayumi Kurama[/b] is a rich girl raised by a single father who fulfills her every financial whim. She is successful in everything she does, including drifting. However, if victory is at stake, her friendship with Hatori may be at risk.
[*] [b]Satoru Hayashi[/b] very quickly becomes Scorpion’s main rival. He is cheerful and reckless, but his family is poor, so he does not feel like a part of his school. Satoru’s car belonged to his uncle, a famous drifter. 
[*] [b]Kaori Kato[/b] is Aoi’s best friend. This artistic girl works at a nearby paint shop. Independent and progressive, she always supports Aoi, even if she believes Hatori isn't a good boyfriend.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/d7cc11eee98d74713da0349ef2d9aa09958158f2.png[/img]
[h2]JDM saga[/h2]
The free prologue [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] is an introduction to the story, which will continue in the full version of the game. Your feedback is extremely important to us, so we encourage you to fill in the [url=https://forms.gle/aXhogARNdfggVFAX7]survey[/url] to help us improve the full version of the game. Additionally, we invite you to share your impressions and suggestions on our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] channel.

notes.title: Pyrkon 2024
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

We finally bring you a report from an amazing event - [b]Pyrkon[/b]! This was the first, but certainly not the last event where we had the pleasure of presenting our game, [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/url][/b] live. We encourage you to check out our vlog of the three days of [b]Pyrkon[/b], to see how much fun we had and everything that happened.

[previewyoutube=T9QuOjynkM0;full][/previewyoutube]
The main attraction of our zone was the tent, where stands with computers awaited you for you to test your skills on specially prepared tracks. The competition was fierce until the last minute, and some of you returned on other days to beat your records. During the event, you could take part in two competitions. We prepared two special events: Grip and Drift, the winners of which were rewarded with packages that included:
[list]
[*] JDM T-Shirt,
[*] JDM key lanyard,
[*] an early access to the prologue of JDM: Rise of the Scorpion,
[*] JDM stickers.
[/list]During [b]Pyrkon[/b], we had the opportunity to work with the [b]Jeremiah Kane[/b] band, one of the creators of the music for our game. Our stand featured drift cars, including a very special one wrapped with the character from our prologue - [b]Ayumi[/b]. The pink car with [b]#LetsDrift[/b] stickers and the [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b] logo became quite the attraction, drawing crowds of visitors eager to take photos with it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/34083268e7a7bc503e49a26c64c7a6337bd8e8f3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ae9a1ba5ef3e4e5389a787104d345c125b731789.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8631eb9d9af30c9950823e17948b0be29c52cf78.png[/img]
At the event, we also attended the [b]Game Days Show[/b] conference where our Event Manager had the opportunity to answer many questions from the community. We discussed the upcoming prologue, the manga-style storyline, in-game sounds, and the birth of the collaboration between [b]JDM[/b] and the Jeremiah Kane team. The conference was hosted by Dominik Bos and Krzysztof M. Maj, who brought a lot of energy and professionalism to the event. If you weren't able to join us live, you can watch the entire conference on [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ltZJDq64dNI&ab_channel=KrzysztofM.Maj]Krzysztof M. Maj's[/url] channel (2: 20: 05).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8ba7cc1799aa5326bbdfb26194bf9c49e5220a96.png[/img]
We would like to thank everyone who visited our stand. Your enthusiasm and positive responses were amazing! Some of you had heard of our game before, while others were discovering it for the first time but each of you brought something special with your feedback and good humor. Thanks to you, we know we are on the right track! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/a7d2aa0f13fb3efe77efe9dea7578becbd33adb9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f6e9cd302bb2f8a0bf8b0a21d444e2c55ba6a8b9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/bc91e3ca5d04b8dd4673763d573a668d08a0af1d.png[/img]
Special thanks to [url=https://diablochairs.com/][b]Diablo Chairs[/b][/url] for providing comfortable chairs and desks, and to [url=https://www.facebook.com/hiropcgaming][b]HIRO[/b][/url] for providing the computers and monitors that allowed the game to run smoothly and effectively. Your support was invaluable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/0beed3e5553dd9cfd3da8cb9f80f3529eb8956f4.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/56ad6b97342e473ee9e94879b69d0174659a4472.png[/img]
This was our first event, but certainly not our last. We look forward to future opportunities to meet you in person, share our progress, and celebrate our passion for drifting and Japanese car culture together.

Add the game to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion]wishlist[/url] on Steam and join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] for regular [b]giveaways[/b]. Stay tuned for the latest news and don't miss any surprises! See you there.

notes.title: Let’s Create!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu,[/h1]

Today, we have some information about the characters and art style in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]. Our game is a racing game like no other. Thanks to our team of amazing artists, we merged a classic racing game narrative with a story presented on manga panels. They replace typically used cut scenes and appear throughout the story with each successive event (don’t worry, there will be an option to skip it). From our perspective, the story part is very important because we would like players to feel like a part of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/d7e04fc78ecc8fc16b8d6bab325bed2546295e0e.png[/img]

The upcoming free prologue - [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url], is an introduction to show you what type of storylines and characters we prepared for you in the full version of the game.

[h2]Art of racing[/h2]
We love classics, like Initial D, Akira, Ghost in the Shell and Evangelion. But the style we created in the making of the manga is mostly inspired by the series Gangsta. We draw inspiration from Japanese and American comics and movies. Since we are gamers ourselves and love pop culture, we wanted to add many easter eggs that players will be able to find in our open world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/4cf252cf659321590c5f3ce1327dfb1b04764e37.png[/img]
[h2]Know the characters[/h2]
Each character has their own backstory to tell, so players can learn about their experiences and why they behave in certain ways. Thanks to that, everyone will be able to find someone to identify with. Meet the main cast of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url]:

[h3]Hatori Hasashi, 18 years old. [/h3]
An excellent student and baseball team captain. Raised in a traditional Japanese family. Hatori finds his true calling on the track. His arrogance and pride never allow him to lose a race, but rivals keep coming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/1ba096c88f0a96cd3f216d2ea55f179b2b2b9c75.png[/img]
[h3]Aoi Ishida, 16 years old. [/h3]
Hatori's girlfriend and childhood friend who always supports him, especially in drift. Their parents want them to get married right after Aoi’s 18th birthday. She loves cars and spends a lot of time with Kaori. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3c204d3dc2e464f8317c8b93ea33199dc0fa269f.png[/img]
[h3]Satoru Hayashi, 17 years old.[/h3]
He is not rich and being in a private school is hard for him. Drives without a license with a car from an uncle, who is a famous drifter. Like him, Satoru wants to be the best on the track, so he quickly becomes Hatori’s rival.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ac455bec32fba3f0d465070727896822ea36883a.png[/img]
[h3]Ayumi Kurama, 18 years old.[/h3]
A rich girl raised by a single father who fulfills her every financial whim. Ayumi is a perfectionist, who is successful in every new hobby, especially drift. The adrenaline on track is everything to her, and she treats racing with Hatori like a playground. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/4dda175e525f65df7e965e4b39bbb7314f558882.png[/img]
[h3]Kaori Kato, 17 years old.[/h3]
An artistic soul and an independent girl who works at a nearby paint shop. She’s Aoi’s best friend but she doesn’t like her boyfriend, Hatori. Kaori doesn’t trust him, but she will support her no matter what.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8dca34bcf34e5a6e370fffe6d1b820db7500398c.png[/img]

The art style in JDM changed a lot throughout the production of the game. The first iterations of the characters were inspired by the visual novel style. Eventually, we decided that the designs needed to be more mature. Also, manga pages added more dynamic to the story than visual novel cutscenes. This choice gave us a chance to work with many, amazing artists. Check out the first look at our characters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/d6d253b76d8e2d3e3fdb2c0bbde17db4f94079c5.png[/img]

Right now, we could describe the genre of our manga as seinen (marketed toward young adult men). Every concept changed from the first vision, but we really wanted to ensure that each design would be deeply rooted in the story. 

We’re thrilled with how our character concept art has turned out, but tell us what you think. Next week on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] Steam page we will uncover more information about new locations from the prologue, so stay tuned and follow us there!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/

Remember to add [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] and the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/]free prologue[/url] to your Steam wishlist. Follow JDM [url=https://linktr.ee/japanesedriftmaster]social media[/url] and join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] for future updates and competitions. Get your engines ready for more exciting news very soon.

notes.title: Let's Produce!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

We hope you're ready for the upcoming free prologue [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url], coming in the summer of 2024! To make your wait a little more pleasant, today we're taking you behind the scenes of the car physics work in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM[/b][/url]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/37796abfe460eee1ecfc31e7f0ddde7e1a209ba4.png[/img]

While creating [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url], we pay a lot of attention to detail, as we care about your best driving experience. Recently, we invited professional drifters to the studio. They got behind the wheel of the cars in our game to share their feelings. Together with our programmers, they tested various forms of driving so that the latter could make changes and improvements to the cars' driving physics on an ongoing basis. 

Many thanks to [url=https://www.instagram.com/fiji.raw/]fiji.raw[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/@ShifterDrifter/videos]ShifterDrifter[/url] i [url=https://www.instagram.com/oh_pasiak/]Mateusz Pasiak[/url] for your involvement and accurate feedback. We also invite you to watch the video from our meeting:

[previewyoutube=YIkGG5P6R4g;full][/previewyoutube]
That's not all! In order to best translate drifters' experiences into mechanics in our game, we not only invite them for tests, but also visit them on the track. 

We recently had the opportunity to become one of the sponsors at an event dedicated to Japanese car enthusiasts. Together with [b]JDM Trójmiasto[/b] - organizers of [b]JDM Track Day[/b] - we have prepared something special for the holders of JDM Track Day 2024 - Season Pass. Thanks to [url=https://www.instagram.com/weztonagraj/]weztonagraj[/url] for the amazing shots! The season began on Saturday, May 11, at the Autodrom Pomorze - Driving Technique Improvement Center. Like previous editions, this one was a track workout where participants could show or boost their driving skills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/4b467fa07691de32672093942573e4b9fa64a0c4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/bee1b7013c51674af0e55d8779e50cf53373419e.png[/img]

Thank you for being with us and giving your support. If you would like to meet us live and try out the tracks of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] before the official release, we invite you to this year's [b]Pyrkon[/b] on [b]June 14-16[/b], in Poznan (Poland). Together with the [url=https://www.instagram.com/jeremiahkane_official/]Jeremiah Kane[/url] band, whose songs you can hear in our game, we are preparing for you many activities and contests with prizes. Join our [url=https://www.facebook.com/events/380324237679742/][b]Facebook[/b][/url] event so you won't miss the latest news. Participation in Pyrkon will be our first event, but we assure you that it will not be the last, and what's more - not only in Poland!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/815ff678297a0bfece82c185f4fe283ea7aa0244.png[/img]
That's it for today, but we'll see you soon with another news. Remember to add the prologue of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] and the full version of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM[/b][/url] to your wish list on Steam and join our Discord. notes.title: Let’s Answer!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

It's been a while since we've been here, but we haven't forgotten you! We hope you've missed us a little. Today we come to you with answers to your most burning questions that came up during our last Q&A session on [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/af60ff0aec08c352dd26f4eada9759e1be5e8014.png[/img]

[b]Q: Please let us know when you will reveal the release date.[/b]
A: Unfortunately, we can't reveal a specific date yet, but it will be in the fall of 2024.

[b]Q: When will you reveal the full car list? Are you still adding more cars to the full game?[/b]
A: We will provide information on available cars near the launch and yes, we are constantly working on new cars.

[b]Q: How many km of roads are there in the full map, and how long would you expect to travel from one side of the map to the other?[/b]
A: Tough question, the planned area will be big, in the demo there is about 10-15% of the map. There will also be tracks, events, and other attractions.

[b]Q: I could see a road similar to Akina in Initial D on the map. Will you also have roads similar to Akagi and Irohazaka?[/b]
A: We can't reveal it but know players' expectations.

[b]Q: I am not into drifting, but I love grip touge racing. What percentage of events in the full game will be grip events?[/b]
A: You will certainly not be bored, we are planning various events.

[b]Q: What are your inspirations when you create the game?[/b]
A: Each team member has different inspirations, but mostly we are drift and JDM car enthusiasts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/bef2fa05aaa8f6d2a46beed60c9d0efc44622fc7.png[/img]

[b]Q: Will there be DLCs for the game in the future?[/b]
A: We can't reveal anything officially, but we have plans on how to develop our game in the future.

[b]Q: What feature are you most excited about adding to the game?[/b]
(Certain track? Uncommon car interaction - car wash, tire change? Specific car, etc...)
A: It would be a storyline inside the game, this will be something that will distinguish our title.

[b]Q: What will the maximum capacity of players be in each online lobby?[/b]
A: It's not specified yet, we are still working on it. 

[b]Q: Will there be a ghost car feature to practice tandem drifting offline/solo?[/b]
A: We have a plan for this, however, the game is still in production, so I can't say how it will look.

[b]Q: How many tracks will there be on the initial release? And will more be implemented in future updates/DLC?[/b]
A: We can't reveal that, we are preparing a lot of surprises for players. 

[b]Q: How much will the game cost?[/b]
A: Less than AAA games, we can’t reveal the full price yet. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/caa5a49ebfb9f21260e3cb1c84d7aca105892153.png[/img]

[b]Q: Will there be a prologue or second demo before the release?[/b]
A: We say anything without an official announcement, stay tuned!

[b]Q: Will there be more detailed cockpit animations, such as characters shifting through gears like in Gran Turismo 4?[/b]
A: We are still working on it, but as we show in the demo, there is an animation of characters shifting through gears.

[b]Q: Will there be different exhaust systems that change how the car sounds depending on the exhaust system installed, rather than having just one sound for different exhausts?[/b]
A: It is possible, we have a great sound engineer who does all sorts of wonders with the sounds. 

[b]Q: Will the game be released physically and digitally for PS5/Xbox?[/b]
A: We are focusing on PC at the moment, and consoles afterward.

[b]Q: Will DLSS be integrated 100% in any future of the game?[/b]
A: We can't promise anything. The game is still in production, we are working on many things and features. 

[b]Q: How will the livery system be? In-game editing, or can we upload JPGs/PNGs to the game/ edit them separately in the photo editor of PC?[/b]
A: We are constantly working on the livery editor to meet the expectations of players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/1d3c11dbb00b84685ab6cbfcfb5eba2a10865c7a.png[/img]

[b]Q: Will you update the game simultaneously on GOG and Steam? Or is it possible that one platform gets an update while the other doesn't?[/b]
A: Yes, all platforms will be updated.

[b]Q: Will you add more and more tuning options with updates and give us more and more content?[/b]
A: Yes, after the premiere the game will be kept updated.

[b]Q: Will we be able to switch between weather like rain, snow, etc.?[/b]
A: Yes, there will be a weather system and day/night system.

[b]Q: Will there be a storyline?[/b]
A: Yes, we are preparing something special.

[b]Q: How long will it take until we can use multiplayer?[/b]
A: We're working on it already, it will be a big update to the game. 

If you want to know more about [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url], then be sure to check out the pinned [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1153410/discussions/0/3825289852117423714/][b]FAQ[/b][/url] thread in the Steam Discussions. We've collected all the questions that have come in on our social media since the [b]JDM[/b] demo release. Don't forget to add the game to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]Wish List[/url] on Steam and join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] so you don't miss any news from the world of Japanese drifting. We are preparing something special for you, so stay tuned! Stay tuned.

notes.title: Let’s Visit Japan!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

In today's devlog, we take you on a journey through Japan. One of our devs recently had the opportunity to visit this beautiful cherry blossom country. Our soundman shares his impressions of the trip and how it will influence the work on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]. Let's get started!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/48bd11dca9a30d955879f2da8876a5f8e43ed357.jpg[/img]
[h2]Beauty of Japan[/h2]
Every aspect of the country is radically different from what we are used to in Europe. The architecture, the customs, the vehicles on the roads, the interactions with people, the peace and order on the streets - these and many other elements made our developer's two-week stay in Japan an unforgettable experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8e186b84a0648a0996679179c93a39753b7bf8ad.jpg[/img]
[h2]Magic of sounds[/h2]
As Dawid is the main soundman for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM[/b][/url], this trip was a unique opportunity for him to record the authentic sounds of everyday life in Japan, as well as the sounds of the cars on the track. During the trip, he collected a lot of ambient sounds from the streets and various service locations that are strongly associated with Japanese culture. He also visited world-famous drift tracks (which we discuss below) to record the sounds of cars and bikes competing against each other. In addition to the sound recordings, David actively photographed various elements of the environment to give our graphic designers even more inspiration for their work. This will allow us to create an extraordinary atmosphere in our game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/7ffaddebe51851d64d0459ce736e969d15737d5e.jpg[/img]
[h2]Ebisu[/h2]
Considered by many to be the Mecca of drifting, Ebisu is a legendary complex located in Fukushima Prefecture. It is the perfect place for lovers of controlled drifting. Ebisu Circuit offers up to seven completely different tracks, surrounded by a zoo with rare animals such as the albino lion. The area is not only huge but also features large changes in terrain, adding to the unique atmosphere. It is a meeting place for drift enthusiasts from all over the world who want to hone their skills in a unique atmosphere. Below is a video from our developer's channel of his visit to Ebisu.

[previewyoutube=ngclxtRRjK0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Tsukuba[/h2]
The Tsukuba circuit is the quintessential motorsport circuit. Located in Ibaraki Prefecture, it is 2,045km long. There are grandstands at the corners from where you can comfortably watch your favorite section of the track while listening to live commentary from loudspeakers throughout the venue. It is the perfect venue for time trial enthusiasts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8e690b23207b57375349e046512d0b0387b0cb2e.jpg[/img]
[h2]The dev's story[/h2]
While driving back from Ebis, David experienced an incident that was exceptionally memorable. Slowly adjusting to the traffic on the motorway and adjusting his navigation, he noticed a police car at a signal, suggesting he take the emergency lane. He didn't know exactly what to expect and the language barrier made communication difficult, but with the help of an interpreter, everything was clarified. The police officers' attention was drawn to the slow movement of the road and they wanted to make sure that the car was not damaged or the driver had not fainted. After a short conversation and a few jokes, he continued his journey. To this day, he recalls this unusual interaction with the Japanese police as very pleasant and unexpected.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f8789a7ca442646d059bff1a3ab190f2e37c4f52.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/81c5b36797e56d44756d05d805fe4f0bf1834033.jpg[/img]
Our developer's journey through Japan has opened up a whole new horizon of sounds that are sure to bring a unique atmosphere to our game. The beauty of Japan, captured in sound and image, will allow us to further reflect what makes this country so special. As a reminder, the [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b] demo will only be available until the end of January, so make sure you check it out while there's still time! Add [b]JDM[/b] to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]wishlist[/url] on Steam and visit us on [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] where we're always here to help. See you there!

notes.title: Let’s Tune!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

We've received a lot of messages from you regarding car tuning in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url], so here comes a new devlog. Today, we'll delve into various modification options and explain how to set things up for an enjoyable ride. We'll start with a brief description of two in-game events, how to adjust your vehicle for them, and then move on to more detailed settings. Let’s tune!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/524fb145f07ee27598d57c2bc4f05e74483cc4a5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Drift Event[/h2]
In a [i]drift event[/i], the goal is to score as many points as possible for controlled drifting. Factors include speed, angle of drift, and drift length. Uninterrupted drifts also earn a combo multiplier, crucial for achieving the best score.
Configuring your car here is largely a matter of personal preference, but controlled drifting requires breaking traction—there's no one-size-fits-all recipe. Seek an optimal balance between grip and power to maintain the drift without sacrificing too much traction.
PS. In this case, the steering angle is your friend—the more, the better! ;)

[h2]Grip Event[/h2]
A [i]grip event[/i] is the opposite of a drift event—here, the focus is on reaching the finish line as quickly as possible. You'll encounter events where you need to achieve the shortest lap time and classic races against opponents to be the first to cross the finish line.
Similarly, configuring your car here is mostly a matter of personal preference, but generally, the more grip you set, the better.

[h2]Realism[/h2]
In the game, you can modify various mechanical and visual parts, much like in real life. Spoilers or additional aerodynamic parts can noticeably alter the car's drag and downforce while modifying the exhaust affects both performance and sound. You'll have access to a full range of parts with different impacts on your car. Of course, at the beginning, you might not afford "top-shelf" parts and may need to save up or settle for "basic" modifications.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f1c6c565230618c0b5b50cf176fa41c714f90aa5.jpg[/img]
[h2]Steering[/h2]
[i]Steering angle[/i], the angle of rotation, is the maximum possible turn of the wheels in degrees. Drifters desire this because it allows for high-angle drifting and helps recover when things get a bit too wild. Remember that suspension primarily influences handling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8d8aa5aa54e5056c55aad3b0b7dc3fd9e47adaa3.jpg[/img]
[h2]Gearbox[/h2]
Smart gear ratio changes will give you what you need from your car. Shorter ratios make the car accelerate faster and initiate drifts more easily, while longer ratios result in a higher top speed but take longer to reach it. Like with everything, moderation is key, and too short or too long ratios can do more harm than good.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/cbe8a125269b10ae0c062caa5d4a756ca68ca5b1.jpg[/img]
[h2]Differential[/h2]
When a car takes a turn, the inner wheel covers a shorter distance than the outer wheel. To maintain stability, the inner wheel must rotate more slowly. The [i]differential mechanism[/i] ensures it receives a smaller portion of the torque and slows down, allowing the outer wheel to spin faster. This helps the car navigate turns smoothly.

Setting the differential to 100% means both wheels always rotate at the same speed, transmitting the same torque to both. This is particularly desirable in drifting and lets you unleash the engine's potential. In time trials (grip), it might not be necessary, as the car could become too oversteer. For grip, a less aggressive differential setting is usually better. Like with suspension, it's an individual choice, and there's no definitive answer to what settings are better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/207a5093719b8611e71ddde3c35997db43398f38.jpg[/img]
[h2]Brakes[/h2]
[i]Brake pressure[/i] is simply the force applied by the brakes. While one might think more is better, excessive pressure can be a hindrance, hence the ability to adjust it. [i]Brake balance[/i] refers to the distribution of braking forces between the front and rear axles. The default balance is 75% to the front and 25% to the rear, influencing the car's behavior and stability during braking. Adjusting this balance entirely to the front allows the car to burn rubber with ease but can lead to significant understeer during corner braking. As for handbrake force, the more, the better for drifters, as it makes locking the wheels easier. :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/a8c4cb3b4f1b8dd7b96744db6adb7b47748615ca.jpg[/img]
[h2]Wheels[/h2]
Wheels are the direct link between the car and the road, significantly influencing its handling. Wider tires mean more grip, and to fit wider tires, you need wider rims—visual changes here go hand in hand with changes in handling.

Greater grip is an advantage in time trials, but drifting, it requires more power to induce a drift. Aside from size, the tire model is also crucial, as they differ in grip under various conditions. 

Theoretically, a wider wheelbase means more grip, but unlike changes in tire width, it's an almost imperceptible change. The wheelbase allows us to "push" the wheel outward, mainly for visual aesthetics, so the wheel aligns nicely with the fender width. If we can't afford to mount a sufficiently wide rim that aligns with the fender or if it would excessively increase the car's grip, spacers come to the rescue, helping "push" the wheel without changing its width.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/b75a09a55329414205d756c621f7c1389130e250.jpg[/img]
As many experts as there are, there are opinions. When customizing your car for drifting, it's essential to be guided by your preferences and experiment to find that "golden mean." We hope we've shed some light on the tuning options in [b]JDM[/b], and that the information from this devlog proves useful. Thanks for all the messages that come to us every day. We're here for you, and our goal is to create a game that satisfies all drift fans. Visit our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discorda[/url], and remember to add [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b] to your Steam [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/ ]wishlist[/url]. Until next time.

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

It's been a while since we released the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] demo and Halloween update.
In response to your feedback, we came back today with a new update and livestreaming! We hope you enjoy the new features and honor us with your presence during today's stream.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/0a75de27c556280bb6171a1be9570a6156025a02.jpg[/img]

[h2]Device support[/h2]
Now you can take full control of your steering wheel and not worry about compatibility, as we are introducing support for all popular steering wheels today. Controller lovers can use a variety of pads, including [i]Xbox[/i] and [i]PlayStation[/i], and fans of classic keyboard gameplay can enjoy the game on any model!

If you experience any problems, please get in touch with us by email at [b]support@jdmgame.com[/b] or report a bug on our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/53fccec45e7e85ce1f369b43a569e60e7564fd9c.jpg[/img]
[h2]Key mapping[/h2]
More than one avid gamer will be pleased with this option. Well-configured and properly assigned button functions are the key to satisfying drifting, and now you can customize them to suit your driving style! Your rules, your drift! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ed74f595da2d681dcafb661c6879678af04aeb42.jpg[/img]
[h2]Optimisation[/h2]
We have received countless messages from you asking us to improve the optimization of the game, so this day has come. We've managed to improve the performance of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM[/b][/url] to some extent, but remember that this is a demo version and we're constantly working to give you the best possible experience. 

The settings allow you to choose from low, medium, high and ultra presets to adjust your gameplay. If the game is not running properly, we recommend lowering the graphics settings. We hope that this update will greatly enhance your driving experience and enjoyment and that nothing will stand in your way of becoming a true Japanese drift master! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/84410d214507bf0db5b9b29d01be457ee1d12a81.jpg[/img]

First of all, we would like to thank you for the warm welcome [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/ ][b]DEMO Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]! [b]Over 2,000[/b] players worldwide played the [b]JDM[/b] demo yesterday, which exceeded our expectations by far. We would like to thank you for this and for joining our livestream where, despite initial sound and connection issues, we had a great time together.

[url=https://forms.gle/BAKm1wVozUyKh91FA][h2]Survey[/h2][/url] We have received an extremely high number of positive comments and suggestions from you. We are striving to create a game that meets the expectations of all players, so every opinion is very important to us. If you have already had a chance to play the DEMO, please fill in the [url=https://forms.gle/BAKm1wVozUyKh91FA][b]survey[/b][/url] that we have prepared for you, as any feedback is very valuable to us!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/89987af4bebb129874090ba58bf7790f1107ecdf.jpg[/img]
[h2]Issues and bugs[/h2]
We are aware of the bugs that have appeared in the DEMO and thank you for sending us any bugs or problems you encounter. The first release of the trial version is just the beginning and we will continue to update it. Below are some of the recurring issues that you have reported to us.
 
[h3]FATAL ERROR / Crash[/h3]
The most common issue - [i]Fatal Error[/i] means that your hardware is too weak to play our game. 
Currently, the minimum and recommended requirements are:

[b]MINIMUM[/b]:
Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
OS: 64-bit Windows 10
Processor: Ryzen 5 2600 or i5-7400
Memory: 8 GB RAM
Graphics: GeForce GTX1660 or Radeon RX580 8GB
DirectX: Version 12
Storage: 16 GB available space

[b]RECOMMENDED[/b]:
Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
OS: 64-bit Windows 10
Processor: Ryzen 5 3600 or intel i5 10400f
Memory: 32 GB RAM
Graphics: GeForce RTX3060Ti or AMD Radeon RX6700
DirectX: Version 12
Storage: 16 GB available space

If you meet the above requirements and still have trouble launching the game, please send us your system specification (Hardware/System Info, GPU/CPU, RAM, Windows Ver, DirectX)  and the contents of the folder - CrashReportClient in the form of a zip, which is available at the given path: C:User\AppData\Local\JDM\Saved\Crashes to the address [b]support@jdmgame.com[/b]. 

[i]Make sure that you will send us all the data otherwise we won't be able to check this issue.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/c85ac2188c00f69b5b7058f212e8f009a6b51c83.jpg[/img]
[h2]Upcoming update[/h2]
We are currently focusing on improving performance and compatibility, and we are aware of the issues you are experiencing, so we are preparing updates for you. 
[list]
[*] A priority for us is to introduce support for more steering wheels. At this time, we are fully confident that the game will work correctly on the G29/G920 Logitech (without additional accessories) and T300rs (without additional accessories).
[*] The VR bug will also be fixed by us. 
[/list] Please keep in mind that the PS4 controller[b] is not[/b] supported by us and it is completely random, if the controller works for someone, it may still not work for someone else. We are currently working on expanding the devices we support. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/2284454fafec477a2152c227dd4d56904a9c5644.jpg[/img]
[h2]Discord[/h2]
Thank you again for experiencing the DEMO launch with us. We will do our best to provide you with a title that will fully satisfy you. If you have any suggestions, feedback, or just want to chat with other drift fans or show off your [b]JDM[/b] records, then please visit our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url]. We currently have over 12,000 active members like this, so go ahead and join our community.

We would also like to remind you that on [b]Thursday (12th October) at 10 PM CEST [/b] there will be a second [b]livestreaming[/b] of the game where you can talk to us. notes.title: Let's Project!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Today, we're taking you on a walkthrough of the interface development process for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url]. The UI (User Interface) is an extremely important element, so we want to share with you the design choices and challenges we have encountered during its creation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/92e8088c8344b1361608e1fdd169124a955adfb5.jpg[/img]
[h2]Essentials[/h2]
It is important to remember that a game is, first and foremost, a product to be used. So when designing the interface, usability comes first. We want players to be able to get to the place or option they want quickly and efficiently, without being taken out of the rhythm and atmosphere of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/fa1fa673587c414381f39cfce65cd1b92cc07071.jpg[/img]
[h2]Inspirations[/h2]
When designing the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM[/b][/url] interface, we drew a lot of inspiration from Japanese pop culture, including anime and manga, as well as the extensive drift and car culture. We want our production to reflect the true atmosphere of the Cherry Blossom Country and provide you with as much fun as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/a8a337063745372344776d92333f7559af785e64.jpg[/img]
[h2]Challenges[/h2]
The options in the game are very extensive and have a lot of settings. We can configure, buy, sell cars, and we have many modes to choose from. The same goes for the menus. We were challenged by the variety of options and yet, we wanted everything to be consistent and clear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/548ad9e4c265e8cb3b092b8d8f692f6512b3865f.jpg[/img]
[h2]Cooperation[/h2]
In graphic design, it is crucial to maintain good communication between several departments. The UX department, which deals with usability, passes this information on to the designer, who combines it into a single, coherent graphical style. A smooth flow of information and an understanding of how the graphics work in the game engine will ensure that production runs smoothly and without unnecessary misunderstandings. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/83c7a2c2a07a6b5c50c4d84b2eedbe53fbe76081.jpg[/img]
We hope that this behind-the-scenes look at the interface design has given you a few tidbits of information and insight into the work we put into [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b]. If you want to keep up to date with the latest news, join us on [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url], where you can communicate directly with us and share your insights and ideas. It's a great place for true drift fans! Also, don't forget to add [b]JDM[/b] to your Steam [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]wishlist[/url] so you don't miss any updates.

Thank you for your support and for being part of our community. See you in the next devlog!

notes.title: Let’s Record!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Today we take you behind the scenes of the sound creation process for [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]Japanese Drift Master[/url][/b]! We've put together an amazing journey through the process for you to see and hear how the sounds of engines, crashes, and collisions are created. So sit back and buckle up, because here we go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/edadc0de483fcc2104753bcf58c7c2e882c3fcf5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Process[/h2]
We record the cars with a combination of microphones from different brands. During the session, we record elements of the car such as the engine, air intake, different perspectives of the exhaust, and the interior. All the tracks are processed in a special program that creates assets using effects and processes, which can then be modified and efficiently implemented into a coherent whole. This gives us complete freedom when it comes to rendering sound in the game. We can decide how much we want to hear from each element of the car, which is useful for the different driving angles, for example. For example, a view from the front bumper will sound different to a view from outside the car.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/e3610252a27fd0fcccd8503067049ea47742853d.jpg[/img]
[h2]Diversity[/h2]
The sound inside the car is achieved by creating a separate mix for all the audio in the game. Both the sounds of the engine, exhaust, and what happens outside the car (collisions, ambiance, tire squeal) go through processes that simulate the space inside the car. Special samples are recorded to allow us to do this. This gives us complete freedom to work and does not force us to create different sets of sounds for the camera outside and inside the car. As for what happens outside, we try to make it interesting, both sonically and visually. Our artists have created a very atmospheric world, which we try to enhance with sound. As a curiosity, we would add that a lot of the recording was done in Japan, but that's a story for another post. ;).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/8753879962044bef76b9ef4da10786f0848a861f.jpg[/img]
[h2]Challenges[/h2]
One of the characteristics of car games is that they have a pre-defined sound framework. When creating the audio for a model of an existing car, it would be good to reflect its actual sound, especially if the title is also aimed at car enthusiasts. Access to some vehicles is quite limited, and the matter is even more difficult if you are looking for a production model without any modifications that would affect the sound. Creating a realistic sound for a large number of different cars and balancing this with our vibrant, open world is by far our biggest challenge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/eabc82c1773e6d4f56cb33c355daa67e3b61e398.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Let’s Design!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Hello again! Today we are going to introduce you to the part of a team working on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url], more specifically our [i]Designers[/i]! Each of them has an important role in our project, as our game has an open world. We would like to take this opportunity to introduce you to them and their work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/c1e5c5e83f9ee0a89174c7567ed7055cb3ee0908.jpg[/img]
[h2]Damian[/h2]
3D Graphic Designer with over 12 years of experience. He started his career creating architectural visuals and spent the next 7 years working as a 3D modeler for TurboSquid, where he gained experience in texturing, mapping, and rendering. In 2016 he started working in game development, on ambitious projects like "Arktika.1 VR", "Metro Exodus" and "Memories Of Mars". At [b]JDM[/b], his main task is to fill the world with realistic 3D models, creating routes and tracks that take your breath away! He has a long-standing interest in Japan and is a fan of manga and anime, so titles such as Initial D and Wangan Midnight are no strangers to him! The biggest challenge he faced with [b]JDM[/b] was finding a balance, as there are a lot of ideas, but as they say - sometimes you have to make some compromises ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/54a157e454946481941f16f112e9dcde81d274da.jpg[/img]
[h2]Tomasz[/h2]
Enthusiastic about cars, photography, video, and editing. His adventure with 3D graphics began with racing games. At [b]JDM[/b], he was initially only involved in creating car models, but as he acquired new knowledge and skills, it was time to play with the Unreal Engine. Currently, he is mainly involved in level design and creating objects that best reflect the charm and atmosphere of Japan. Using the experience gained from many hours of playing sim racing games, he tries to get the best possible shapes and gradients for the corners, which also involves dozens of runs of such sequences - all to your utmost satisfaction. At every stage of development, he spends a lot of time looking at and analyzing Japanese areas and buildings in order to recreate them in the best possible way in the game. As he has said himself, he pays great attention to the smallest details to ensure that [b]JDM[/b] is appreciated and warmly welcomed by all racing game enthusiasts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/00480581fabe73fa7e2bf02f62ea7ce8e56817d4.jpg[/img]
[h2]Jakub “Vorthan”[/h2]
Gaming enthusiast, member of a former eSports team in League of Legends. Working on [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b], this is his debut as a level designer. He first became interested in 3D graphics during his studies but knew immediately that this was what he wanted to do with his career. His work is mainly driven by his imagination and creativity, and there is always a touch of madness in the areas he is responsible for. In his spare time, he volunteers at various conventions and has been one of the organizers of Skiercon for the past two years. He has also taken up cosplay and continues to develop his passions and interests. 
Fot. [url=https://www.facebook.com/celestial.perception.of.vitae]Vitae[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f9fc6f9dc168049f0874888b0c193e9fbb598726.jpg[/img]
[h2]Dawid [/h2]
Sound designer with 10 years of experience, creator of some of the sounds for JDM. His credits include the vehicle recording for Cyberpunk 2077. Of the titles that have had a major influence on his work, NFS Underground 2 is definitely at the top of the list. It is this project that has now led him to dedicate himself to working on virtual cars. With the purchase of a Mazda MX-5 (later RX-8), which he drives in Time Attack mode at various track events - including the JDM Track Day, which he co-organizes - motoring has finally entered his life. He has a long-standing interest in Japanese culture, food and continues to perfect his art of cooking ramen. When asked what he found most challenging about the project, he replied, "There are more challenges in making a JDM than there are in making limited editions of the Miata (if you are interested in Mazdas, this joke is for you). Classically, with sound, the biggest problem is creating a coherent world to emphasize the overall atmosphere of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ac5f113599dbf37a8abbdb6e0fa2f804dbe5164a.jpg[/img]
[h2]Adam [/h2]
3D/2D graphic designer with 22 years of experience. He started printing, and designing fridges while developing his skills in modeling and creating architectural visuals. In his career, he has created 2D illustrations along with assets for hidden object games, 3D assets, and concept art. In 2015, he landed at Vivid Games, where he developed his expertise in game optimization, character creation, and UI. He has been immersed in the world of games since the '80s when he discovered titles such as Super Hang On and R-type, but his biggest inspiration came from the games Final Fantasy 7 and Gran Turismo, which introduced him to the atmosphere and culture of Japan. A big fan of Japanese cars, including the Mazda RX7 and Honda NSX. He has been involved with Japanese Drift Master from the beginning and his main task is to create the world, where he tries to replicate the real locations as well as possible. In addition, he is responsible for all the trees, and plants in the game as well as creating the UI, assets, props, and buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/2606af37928b034af62c45b7dd008a7d8567a2a3.jpg[/img]
[h2]Przemysław[/h2]
The 3D and 2D graphic designer who started his adventure with sim-racing. He managed to create several cars based on laser scanning technology, as well as a full-scale Polish racetrack. For the last few years, he has been developing his skills as a graphic artist and designer. In [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b] he is responsible for the cars, tuning parts, as well as the creation and quality of the presented world. Privately, he is a lover of motoring, reworking, and restoring old cars. In the devlog [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/3662037536268760285]"Let's Scan"[/url], you will find more information about its work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/9fee7fec18bebd3ce5cb25ead5aaf3693d74025b.jpg[/img]
[h2]Arnold [/h2]
Known as BananaBoy, a fan of Japanese car culture, an amateur drifter and mechanic, and owner of several [b]JDM[/b] cars. He has never been involved in game development before but wants to share his true automotive passion in his work. You can read more about his interests and hobbies in the previous [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/3675551506147348072]devlog[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/563cb36f4e8cdc2cf3964b7b4ace657f79a051e4.jpg[/img]
Our game is made first and foremost out of passion and love for cars and Japan. As mentioned in our answers, we are not a AAA studio that produces a lot of titles, our dream is to create and develop our game together with the players. [b]Japanese Drift Master [/b]is more than just a game to us personally, and we hope that after the release you will see how much heart we have put into this production.

If you want to talk to our developers, you can join our [url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] where you can ask them questions and make suggestions. Remember to add [b]JDM[/b] to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]wishlist[/url] on Steam to stay up to date! See you in the next devlog.

notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Welcome back, everyone! If you follow [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]Japanese Drift Master’s[/b][/url] social media channels, you may have seen Tuesday's post teasing today's devlog! We want to showcase the achievements and hobbies of one of our developers who recently took part in a drifting competition! Our team puts a lot of effort into making sure our game replicates drifting mechanics as closely as possible, so taking part in this event was an excellent opportunity to observe and learn. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/c9470f5ffc35bee3ba2886324aaf1f38caa1fe46.jpg[/img]
[h2]What is Next Level Drift?[/h2]
Next Level was born out of a passion for the most exciting and spectacular art of motoring - drifting. The Polish group aims to bring back the original roots of drifting, i.e., aggressive driving combined with unique car styling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/f403803236738af66409e5932a24c0f3a81e7654.jpg[/img]
[h2]Event[/h2] 
Last weekend, i.e. 22-23.07, an international drifting event took place at Autodrom Jastrząb - the most modern automotive training facility in Poland. The style was at the forefront, so you could meet many beautiful, lowered, and aesthetically pleasing cars in a truly Japanese atmosphere!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3b9084820c0f8baf58e08c082c73f1acaea20ac6.jpg[/img]
[h2]Japanese Drift Master[/h2]
The event featured one of our devs, [url=https://www.instagram.com/__bananaboy__/][i]BananaBoy[/i][/url], who has been around the drift community for a good couple of years. His car won the award for best drift car! It is worth mentioning that he built his car, especially for this event over a period of three weeks, staying up all night to combine his hobby with work. We are very proud of his achievement! There was also an element of our production, as you can find stickers from [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master/]Japanese Drift Master[/url][/b] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/gamingfactory][b]Gaming Factory[/b][/url] on [i]BananaBoy[/i]'s car!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/fbefbcad18247deb6c7717414e52e7d45b4acd5b.jpg[/img]
As you may already know, we are constantly working on the demo version of our game, which will be released very soon. We are working hard to bring you the best entertainment and real Japanese style drifting right from the start! We encourage you to join our [url=url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] where you can share suggestions, your own cars and achievements with other drift fans! Join us for a special streaming of gameplay from the [b]JDM[/b] game today [b](20 July) at 12:30 PM PDT (9:30 PM CEST) on Steam[/b]. Buckle up and get ready for a rough ride! We will provide you with another dose of beautiful drifting and astonishing sights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/df6898824ea50d8e9367ec5c2c9e2557b3afb458.jpg[/img]
[h2]Q&A[/h2]
We have answered your most frequently asked questions and collected them in one place - we appreciate the many questions and suggestions. We hope this devlog will clear up some of your doubts, and if you haven't read the previous ones, we encourage you to do so.

[b]Q&A part 1[/b] https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/5529901770445755298
[b]Q&A part 2[/b] https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/3691307763197579839 
[b]Q. Do you plan to do only JDM cars, if so will there be different tuning styles?[/b]
A. No, not just JDM cars. We plan to have different models from different parts of the world and many different tuning styles, so everyone can choose their favorite style of car to drift or just drive through the game.

[b]Q. Are you going to have a sign-up to people can play early access?[/b]
A. There will be a free demo, so everyone can see what is our game about and give us some feedback.

[b]Q. Will you add the anime decal character in the JDM?[/b] 
A. Our team consists of fanatics of automobiles and anime so exciting combinations of styles and an engaging story await players!

[b]Q. How many people are working on the game?[/b]
A. We are not a AAA studio, so our team is under a hundred people.

[b]Q. Will there be a custom mp3 feature where you can import your own music into the game?[/b]
A. No, at the moment we have a planned radio system with a very extensive playlist of our choice. You can check out the tracks on our [url=https://open.spotify.com/playlist/7ErhMg9jw0dcjcmXo7XC73?si=652780e52ada4206]Spotify[/url]. We are constantly trying to expand it with new genres.

[b]Q. How long has this game been in development for?[/b]
A. The game has been in development for several years, we decided to announce it because we are closer to its completion.

[b]Q. Will there be customizable license plates?[/b]
A. At the moment we cannot promise anything, we have plans to do it, but it is not a priority. 

[b]Q. Will the game be released on phones or VR?[/b]
A. At the moment we are focusing on the PC version.

[b]Q. Will the game have any objective and not just a free-roam game that we can chill? Any ideas for map expansions after the release date?[/b]
A. Yes, the game will have a story and characters that the player can relate to. We put a lot of emphasis on the story. There is a development plan for the game, which we will finally announce ;)

notes.title: Let’s Scan!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

In our latest devlog, we are diving into the exciting world of creating cars for the [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b]! The whole process will be explained by Przemek - an automotive enthusiast with a passion for old cars - who is in charge of scanning the cars and parts to be used in the game. Let's rev up the engines and embark on this amazing journey of creation!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3be680ff55f46137da0db0b39b016a6def882c70.jpg[/img]
[h2]Creation process[/h2]
To get a good representation of the cars in the game, we rely on reverse engineering - aided by 3D scanning of real cars. First of all, we have to mat the chrome or find a base in the right condition. Once the digital data has been collected and pre-processed, we can create a detailed model. The final step is to visualize the car in the engine with the necessary animations. For example, we can lower the window to hear the sound of the engine. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/281d13e78d4e9f8f63835c921d333deeef87ae05.jpg[/img]
[h2]Challenges[/h2]
The biggest challenge in producing a car is the time it takes for a small team to create it - a 3D model and sounds are one thing - the car still needs to be driven to get it to behave properly. We base this on real suspension geometry, so cars drive differently after suspension tuning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/3857d5ba8ad89c02d1ba720a4fb91408b1e318a1.jpg[/img]
[h2]Knowledge and style[/h2]
The people in our team are drift fans and actively participate in drifting events. We are in constant contact with professional drifters and the JDM scene - we listen to their comments because they are the most valuable. We try to keep most of the tuning content in the spirit of JDM, which is the most important thing for us, and some of the car modifications are very close to their track counterparts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/01e91946547281a052bc93fc9b5868253c229649.jpg[/img]
We hope you enjoyed today's devlog and we have provided you with some entertainment. Remember to add [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b] to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/Japanese_Drift_Master]wishlist[/url] on Steam and join us on [url=url=https://discord.gg/44VFMPTVtb]Discord[/url] where you can ask us any questions you may have.

notes.title: Let’s Answer More!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Welcome to our second Q&A session! We saw that you enjoyed the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1153410/view/5529901770445755298]last devlog[/url] with answers, so today we come back with another dose of interesting information! We're excited to share even more insights into the development of the [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b]. Let's get started!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/dbb699192ec4973f717befed5898eb89ca1a80fb.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: Where does the game take place?[/b]
A: In JDM, you'll explore the tourist areas around Haikama Lake which was created by our team. 

[b]Q: Will there be traffic in the game? [/b]
A: Yes, other vehicles will also drive around the map.

[b]Q: Is there any weather system?[/b]
A: Yes, there will be sun, clouds, rain, etc. but the main season is summer.

[b]Q: Are there day and night cycles?[/b]
A: Yes, the passage of time is dynamic, there is a full cycle of day and night.

[b]Q: Are only drift events available in the game?[/b]
A: No, there will be also race events and others.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/71cf1ed4ba4338263e406ea3570707bdb293938c.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: Is there an available car list?[/b]
A: Not at the moment.

[b]Q: Will the police chase us?[/b]
A: There is no plan at the moment but maybe we will add something connected to the police chase in the future. 

[b]Q: Will there be paint and tuning shops?[/b]
A: Yes, you will be able to adjust the cars, their exterior, wheels, and interior. Also, there will be an option to paint the car and parts like wheels in the color you like. In further development, we want to add a special system for stickers, etc. 

[b]Q: Is there a damage model in the game?[/b]
A: We do not plan mechanical damage to cars, there will only be simple visual damage and scratches on the texture.

[b]Q: Does the tuning give only a visual aspect? [/b]
A: No, it changes the way you drive the car, physics, etc. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/daa9a19bc69eeecf948cf7acaffb84976c9846ce.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: What’s the game physics, it’s from another game?[/b]
A: No, the physics in the game is our proprietary system.

[b]Q: Can we change the view in the game?[/b]
A: Yes, in the game there will be cameras like close pursuit, far pursuit, from the bumper, from the hood, from the roof, from the cockpit, eyes/inside view.

[b]Q: Can we look around in the game?[/b]
A: It will be possible to look around from inside and outside the car.

[b]Q: Will there be any music in the game?[/b]
A: Yes, we are currently cooperating with music producer Naski but there will be more artists. 

[b]Q: Will this game be compatible with Thrustmaster controllers?[/b]
A: Yes, we support steering wheels eg T300RS.


We hope you enjoyed the second part of our Q&A session. notes.title: Let’s Answer!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ossu![/h1]

Welcome to our latest devlog! Today, we have something special for you - a Q&A session to give you an inside look into the development of [b]Japanese Drift Master[/b]. From the gameplay mechanics to the story. We answer your burning questions and take you inside our adrenaline-pumping drifting game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/01fe9b7bfb1466a92fcd9dc3ea8e62f701b2ca16.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: What is JDM: Japanese Drift Master?[/b]
A: Welcome to the world's drift mecca – Japan. The game goal is to introduce the atmosphere of Japanese automotive culture and explore the roads where the drift was born. 

[b]Q: What genre is this game?[/b]
A: Simcade with friendly controls that will satisfy fans of more realistic games – although it is accessible enough to enjoy the game also to less experienced players.

[b]Q: When will the game come out?[/b]
A: There is no specific date but our goal is to release the game within the year in early access.

[b]Q: What is the game engine?[/b]
A: Unreal Engine 4

[b]Q: Is there any demo?[/b]
A: We are currently working on a demo version, so stay tuned for more information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/68b02a1965e134fc55f08484b943fc843175e407.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: What about console releases?[/b]
A: At the moment we are focusing on the PC version but we do not exclude console versions in the future. 

[b]Q: Is there any in game story?[/b]
A: In the game, players will find a unique plot that combines elements of racing games from the west with visual novel storytelling from the east. Play through a story about a foreigner who wants to make a name for himself on the Japanese drifting scene.

[b]Q: Is there an open world in the game?[/b]
A: Yes, miles of diverse roads inspired by real and well-known locations from Japan await you.

[b]Q: What’s up with those car sounds?[/b]
A: While playing JDM, you’ll hear original car sounds, both recorded and implemented by our team, using unique technology, created specifically for this project.

[b]Q: Will there be multiplayer?[/b]
A: Yes, after release we will work on the multiplayer mode. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/ea2bb731b6f246e94bd5bd7ffdaa6899c9bcd9c3.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: How much will the game cost?[/b]
A: There is no price yet. 

[b]Q: What control devices will I be able to use?[/b]
A:  You can use a gamepad, steering wheel, or keyboard.

[b]Q: Will there be a photo mode?[/b]
A: Yes, we plan to add the photo mode to the game. 

[b]Q: Who is the producer of the game?[/b]
A: The game is developed by Gaming Factory.

[b]Q: Are you planning to make playtests?[/b]
A: We can't reveal anything at the moment.

[b]Q: Are you planning to support mods?[/b]
A: Yes, in further development there is a plan to support mods.
